title.zh: 卷五十九 列傳第九: 屈突通 任瓌 丘和 許紹 李襲志 姜謩
title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 9: Qu Tutong, Ren Gui, Qiu He, Xu Shao, Li Xizhi, Jian Mo
title.raw: 卷五十九 列傳第九: 屈突通 任瓌 丘和 許紹 李襲志 姜謩 Volume 59 Biographies 9: Qu Tutong, Ren Gui, Qiu He, Xu Shao, Li Xizhi, Jian Mo

sentences.zh: 屈突通 子壽 少子詮 詮子仲翔

translations.literal: Qu Tutong; his son Shou; younger son Quan; Quan's son Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tutong; his son Shou; his younger son Quan; and Quan's son Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 任瑰 丘和 子行恭 行恭子神勣許紹 孫力士 力士子欽寂 欽明 紹次子智仁 少子圉師

translations.literal: Ren Gui; Qiu He; He's son Xinggong; Xinggong's son Shenji; Xu Shao; Shao's grandson Lishi; Lishi's sons Qinji and Qinming; Shao's second son Zhiren; younger son Yusshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui; Qiu He; He's son Xinggong; Xinggong's son Shenji; Xu Shao; Shao's grandson Lishi; Lishi's sons Qinji and Qinming; Shao's second son Zhiren; and his younger son Yusshi.

sentences.zh: 李襲志 弟襲譽子懷亻嚴 姜謩 子行本 行本子簡 簡子晞 簡弟柔遠 柔遠子皎 晦 皎男慶初

translations.literal: Li Xizhi; his younger brother Xizhi's son Huai Yan; Jiang Mo; Mo's son Xingben; Xingben's son Jian; Jian's son Xi; Jian's younger brother Rouyuan; Rouyuan's son Jiao; Jiao's son Hui; Jiao's grandson Qingchu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xizhi; his younger brother Xizhi's son Huai Yan; Jiang Mo; Mo's son Xingben; Xingben's son Jian; Jian's son Xi; Jian's younger brother Rouyuan; Rouyuan's son Jiao; Jiao's son Hui; and Jiao's grandson Qingchu.

sentences.zh: 屈突通，雍州長安人。

translations.literal: Qu Tutong was a native of Chang'an in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tutong came from Chang'an in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 父長卿，周邛州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Changqing was Inspector of Qiongzhou under the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changqing had served as inspector of Qiongzhou under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 通性剛毅，志尚忠愨，檢身清正，好武略，善騎射。

translations.literal: Tutong was by nature fierce and resolute, devoted in heart to loyalty and integrity, disciplined himself in purity and uprightness, fond of military strategy, and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong was fierce and resolute by nature, devoted to loyalty and integrity, strict with himself in conduct, fond of military strategy, and skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為親衛大都督，文帝遣通往隴西檢覆群牧，得隱藏馬二萬餘匹。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era he served as Grand Commander of the Imperial Guard; Emperor Wen sent Tutong to Longxi to inspect the state herds and uncovered more than twenty thousand hidden horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he became grand commander of the imperial guard. Emperor Wen sent him to Longxi to inspect the state herds, where he uncovered more than twenty thousand concealed horses.

sentences.zh: 文帝盛怒，將斬太僕卿慕容悉達及諸監官千五百人，通諫曰：「人命至重，死不再生，陛下至仁至聖，子育群下，豈容以畜產之故，而戮千有餘人？

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and was about to execute the Minister of Studs Murong Xida and fifteen hundred supervising officials. Tutong remonstrated, saying: "Human life is of utmost weight; once dead, one does not live again. Your Majesty is supremely benevolent and supremely sage, nurturing all below as children—how can you, for the sake of livestock, put to death more than a thousand men?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and was about to execute Minister of Studs Murong Xida and fifteen hundred supervising officials. Tutong remonstrated: "Human life is the weightiest of matters; death cannot be undone. Your Majesty is supremely benevolent and sage, nurturing your subjects as children—how can you slaughter more than a thousand men over livestock?

sentences.zh: 愚臣狂狷，輒以死請。」

translations.literal: This foolish minister is rash and obstinate, and ventures to plead with my life."
translations.idiomatic: This foolish minister is rash and obstinate, but I venture to plead with my own life."

sentences.zh: 文帝嗔目叱之，通又頓首曰：「臣一身如死，望免千餘人命。」

translations.literal: The emperor glared and shouted at him; Tutong again bowed his head to the ground and said: "This minister's person is as good as dead; I beg that more than a thousand lives be spared."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor glared and shouted at him. Tutong bowed again and said: "Consider me as good as dead—I beg only that these thousand-odd lives be spared."

sentences.zh: 帝寤，曰：「朕之不明，以至於是。

translations.literal: The emperor came to his senses and said: "My lack of clarity has led to this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to his senses. "My lack of clarity has brought me to this," he said.

sentences.zh: 感卿此意，良用惻然。

translations.literal: I am deeply moved by your intent and truly feel compassion.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply moved by what you have said, and it stirs real compassion in me.

sentences.zh: 今從所請，以旌諫諍。」

translations.literal: Now I grant your request, to honor forthright remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: I grant your request now, to honor forthright remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 悉達等竟以減死論。

translations.literal: In the end Xida and the others were sentenced to commuted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Xida and the others received commuted death sentences.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見委信，擢為右武候車騎將軍。

translations.literal: From this he gradually gained trust and was promoted to Cavalry General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: From this he gradually won the emperor's trust and was promoted to cavalry general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 奉公正直，雖親戚犯法，無所縱舍。

translations.literal: Upholding fairness and uprightness, even when relatives violated the law he showed them no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld fairness and integrity; even when relatives broke the law, he showed them no leniency.

sentences.zh: 時通弟蓋為長安令，亦以嚴整知名。

translations.literal: At the time Tutong's younger brother Gai was magistrate of Chang'an and was likewise known for severity and rigor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his younger brother Gai was magistrate of Chang'an and was likewise famed for severity and rigor.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「寧食三斗艾，不見屈突蓋，寧服三斗蔥，不逢屈突通。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Better to eat three dou of mugwort than to see Qu Tutu Gai; better to swallow three dou of scallions than to meet Qu Tutong."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time had a saying: "Better to eat three dou of mugwort than to see Qu Tutu Gai; better to swallow three dou of scallions than to meet Qu Tutong."

sentences.zh: 為人所忌憚如此。

translations.literal: Such was the dread in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the dread he inspired.

sentences.zh: 及文帝崩，煬帝遣通以詔征漢王諒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Emperor Yang sent Tutong with an edict to summon Prince of Han Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen's death, Emperor Yang sent Tutong with an edict to summon the Prince of Han, Liang.

sentences.zh: 先是，文帝與諒有密約曰：「若璽書召汝，於敕字之傍別加一點，又與玉麟符合者，當就征。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen and Liang had a secret agreement, saying: "If an imperial summons calls you, and beside the character for 'edict' an extra dot is added, and it matches the jade lin tally, then you should come when summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wen and Liang had agreed in secret: "If an imperial summons calls you, look beside the character for 'edict' for an extra dot, and for a matching jade lin tally—only then should you obey the summons."

sentences.zh: 及發書無驗，諒覺變，詰通，通佔對無所屈，竟得歸長安。

translations.literal: When the document was opened and the signs were absent, Liang sensed something amiss and questioned Tutong; Tutong answered by divination without yielding, and in the end was able to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the document arrived without those signs, Liang sensed something was wrong and questioned Tutong. Tutong answered by divination without yielding an inch, and in the end made it back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累轉左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he was repeatedly transferred and became Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he rose through several posts to grand general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 時秦、隴盜賊蜂起，以通為關內討捕大使。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in swarms in Qin and Long, and Tutong was appointed Grand Commissioner for Suppression and Capture within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits swarmed across Qin and Long, Tutong was appointed grand commissioner for suppression and capture within the passes.

sentences.zh: 有安定人劉迦論舉兵反，據雕陰郡，僭號建元，署置百官，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: A man of Anding, Liu Jialun, raised troops in rebellion, seized Diaoyin Commandery, assumed the reign title Jianyuan in usurpation, appointed a full bureaucracy, and had a following of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jialun of Anding raised troops in rebellion, seized Diaoyin Commandery, declared the reign title Jianyuan, set up a full bureaucracy, and gathered a force of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 稽胡首領劉鷂子聚眾與迦論相影響。

translations.literal: Liu Yaozi, a leader of the Ji Hu, gathered a host and acted in concert with Jialun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yaozi, a Ji Hu chieftain, gathered followers and coordinated with Jialun.

sentences.zh: 通發關中兵擊之，師臨安定，初不與戰，軍中以通為怯，通乃揚聲旋師而潛入上郡。

translations.literal: Tutong mobilized troops from within the passes to attack them; when his army reached Anding he at first did not give battle, and the army regarded Tutong as timid. Tutong then proclaimed a withdrawal while secretly entering Shang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong mobilized troops from within the passes to attack them. When his army reached Anding he at first refused battle, and his men took him for timid. He then proclaimed a withdrawal while secretly slipping into Shang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 迦論不之覺，遂進兵南寇，去通七十里而舍，分兵掠諸城邑。

translations.literal: Jialun did not perceive it and thereupon advanced south to raid, encamping seventy li from Tutong and sending detachments to plunder the various cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Jialun never noticed. He marched south to raid, encamped seventy li from Tutong, and sent detachments to plunder towns throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 通候其無備，簡精甲夜襲之，賊眾大潰，斬迦論並首級萬餘，於上郡南山築為京觀，虜男女數萬口而還。

translations.literal: Tutong waited until they were unprepared, selected elite armor, and raided them by night; the rebel host collapsed in great disorder. He beheaded Jialun along with more than ten thousand heads, built a victory mound of skulls on the southern hills of Shang Commandery, and returned with several tens of thousands of captives, men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong waited until they were off guard, picked elite troops, and struck by night. The rebel army collapsed. He killed Jialun and took more than ten thousand heads, built a victory mound of skulls on the southern hills of Shang Commandery, and returned with tens of thousands of captives.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸江都，令通鎮長安。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, he ordered Tutong to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang went to Jiangdu, he left Tutong to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，代王遣通進屯河東。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, the Prince of Dai sent Tutong forward to encamp at Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies rose, the Prince of Dai sent Tutong to advance and encamp at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 既而義師濟河，大破通將桑顯和於飲馬泉，永豐倉又為義師所克。

translations.literal: Before long the righteous army crossed the river and routed Tutong's general Sang Xianhe at Yingma Spring; Yongfeng Granary was also taken by the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the righteous army crossed the river and routed Tutong's general Sang Xianhe at Yingma Spring, and Yongfeng Granary fell to them as well.

sentences.zh: 通大懼，留鷹揚郎將堯君素守河東，將自武關趨藍田以赴長安。

translations.literal: Tutong was greatly afraid; he left the Eagle-Flying Commandant Yao Junsu to defend Hedong and intended to go himself through Wu Pass toward Lantian to reach Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong was terrified. He left Eagle-Flying Commandant Yao Junsu to hold Hedong and planned to take Wu Pass toward Lantian to reach Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 軍至潼關，為劉文靜所遏，不得進，相持月餘。

translations.literal: When the army reached Tong Pass it was blocked by Liu Wenjing and could not advance; the two sides faced each other for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass he was blocked by Liu Wenjing and could not advance; the two sides faced each other for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 通又令顯和夜襲文靜，詰朝大戰，義軍不利。

translations.literal: Tutong again ordered Xianhe to raid Wenjing by night; at dawn a great battle was fought and the righteous army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong ordered Xianhe to raid Wenjing by night. At dawn they fought a great battle, and the righteous army fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 顯和縱兵破二柵，惟文靜一柵獨存，顯和兵復入柵而戰者往覆數焉。

translations.literal: Xianhe loosed his troops and broke two palisades; only Wenjing's one palisade remained. Xianhe's men entered the palisade to fight and came and went several times.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe broke two palisades; only Wenjing's remained. Xianhe's men charged in and out of the palisade again and again.

sentences.zh: 文靜為流矢所中，義軍氣奪，垂至於敗。

translations.literal: Wenjing was struck by a stray arrow; the righteous army's spirit flagged and they were on the verge of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing was struck by a stray arrow. The righteous army's spirit flagged and defeat seemed near.

sentences.zh: 顯和以兵疲，傳餐而食，文靜因得分兵以實二柵。

translations.literal: Xianhe, because his troops were weary, passed rations hand to hand to eat; Wenjing thereby was able to divide troops to fill the two palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe's men were exhausted and passed rations hand to hand. Wenjing used the pause to reinforce his two palisades.

sentences.zh: 又有遊軍數百騎自南山來擊其背，三柵之兵復大呼而出，表裡齊奮，顯和軍潰，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Moreover several hundred mounted scouts came from the southern hills to strike their rear; the troops of all three palisades again shouted and sallied forth, attacking from within and without in concert, and Xianhe's army collapsed—he barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Then several hundred mounted scouts swept down from the southern hills and struck Xianhe's rear. Troops from all three palisades shouted and sallied forth together; attacked from front and rear, Xianhe's army collapsed and he barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 悉虜其眾，通勢彌蹙。

translations.literal: They captured his entire force, and Tutong's situation grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: His entire force was captured, and Tutong's position grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 或說通歸降，通泣曰：「吾蒙國重恩，歷事兩主，受人厚祿，安可逃難？

translations.literal: Someone urged Tutong to surrender. Tutong wept and said: "I have received the state's weighty grace, served two sovereigns, and accepted generous emoluments—how can I flee hardship?
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him to surrender. Tutong wept and said: "I have received the state's deepest favor, served two sovereigns, and drawn generous pay—how can I flee hardship?

sentences.zh: 有死而已！」

translations.literal: There is only death!"
translations.idiomatic: There is only death!"

sentences.zh: 每自摩其頸曰：「要當為國家受人一刀耳！」

translations.literal: He would stroke his own neck and say: "I must yet take a blade for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: He would stroke his own neck and say: "I must yet take a blade for the state!"

sentences.zh: 勞勉將士，未嘗不流涕，人亦以此懷之。

translations.literal: In encouraging and exhorting his officers and men he never failed to shed tears, and for this the men also cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: When he encouraged his officers and men he never failed to weep, and for this they cherished him in turn.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣其家僮召之，通遽命斬之。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent a household servant to summon him; Tutong immediately ordered the man beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent a household servant to summon him; Tutong immediately ordered the man executed.

sentences.zh: 通聞京師平，家屬盡沒，乃留顯和鎮潼關，率兵東下，將趨洛陽。

translations.literal: When Tutong heard that the capital had fallen and his family had all perished, he left Xianhe to garrison Tong Pass and led his army east, intending to hurry to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the capital had fallen and his family was lost, he left Xianhe to hold Tong Pass and marched east toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 通適進路，而顯和降於劉文靜。

translations.literal: Tutong had just set out on the road when Xianhe surrendered to Liu Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely set out when Xianhe surrendered to Liu Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 遣副將竇琮、段志玄等率精騎與顯和追之，及於稠桑。

translations.literal: He sent his deputy generals Dou Cong and Duan Zhixuan and others with elite cavalry, together with Xianhe, in pursuit, and overtook him at Chousang.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy generals Dou Cong and Duan Zhixuan led elite cavalry with Xianhe in pursuit and overtook him at Chousang.

sentences.zh: 通結陣以自固，竇琮縱通子壽令往諭之。

translations.literal: Tutong formed battle lines to secure himself; Dou Cong sent Tutong's son Shou to go and persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong formed battle lines to hold his ground. Dou Cong sent Tutong's son Shou to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 通大呼曰：「昔與汝為父子，今與汝為仇讎。」

translations.literal: Tutong shouted loudly: "Once I was father and son with you; now I am your mortal foe."
translations.idiomatic: Tutong shouted: "Once we were father and son; now we are mortal enemies."

sentences.zh: 命左右射之。

translations.literal: He ordered those beside him to shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to shoot him down.

sentences.zh: 顯和呼其眾曰：「京師陷矣，汝並關西人，欲何所去？」

translations.literal: Xianhe called out to the troops: "The capital has fallen! You are all men of Guanxi—where do you think you are going?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe called to the troops: "The capital has fallen! You are all men of Guanxi—where do you think you are going?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆釋仗。

translations.literal: The multitude all cast down their weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The men all cast down their weapons.

sentences.zh: 通知不免，乃下馬東南向再拜號哭，曰：「臣力屈兵敗，不負陛下，天地神祇，實所鑑察。」

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, Tutong dismounted, bowed twice toward the southeast, and wailed aloud, saying: "Your servant's strength is spent and his army defeated, yet I have not failed Your Majesty—Heaven and Earth and the spirits are my witnesses."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing escape was impossible, Tutong dismounted, bowed twice toward the southeast, and wailed: "My strength is spent and my army defeated, yet I have not failed Your Majesty—Heaven and Earth and the spirits bear witness."

sentences.zh: 遂擒通送於長安。

translations.literal: He was thereupon captured and sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was captured and sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂曰：「何相見晚耶？」

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him: "Why did we meet so late?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said to him: "Why did we meet so late?"

sentences.zh: 通泣對曰：「通不能盡人臣之節，力屈而至，為本朝之辱，以愧代王。」

translations.literal: Tutong wept in reply: "Tutong could not fulfill a minister's full duty; my strength spent, I have come—this is a disgrace to our dynasty and a shame to the Prince of Dai."
translations.idiomatic: Tutong wept in reply: "I could not fulfill a minister's full duty. My strength spent, I have come—this is a disgrace to our dynasty and a shame to the Prince of Dai."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「隋室忠臣也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "A loyal minister of the Sui house."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "A loyal minister of the Sui house."

sentences.zh: 命釋之，授兵部尚書，封蔣國公，仍為太宗行軍元帥長史。

translations.literal: He ordered him released, appointed him Minister of War, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiang, and made him chief secretary to Taizong's campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him released, appointed him minister of war, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiang, and made him chief secretary on Taizong's campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 從平薛舉，時珍物山積，諸將皆爭取之，通獨無所犯。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Xue Ju; at the time rare goods were heaped like mountains and all the generals vied to seize them, but Tutong alone took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Xue Ju. Rare goods were heaped like mountains and every general scrambled for a share, but Tutong took nothing.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而謂曰：「公清正奉國，著自終始，名下定不虛也。」

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he said to him: "You are pure and upright in serving the state, consistent from first to last—your reputation will surely not be empty."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of it he said: "You serve the state with purity and integrity, consistent from first to last—your reputation is well earned."

sentences.zh: 特賜金銀六百兩、彩物一千段。

translations.literal: He specially bestowed six hundred taels of gold and silver and a thousand bolts of colored goods.
translations.idiomatic: He specially bestowed six hundred taels of gold and silver and a thousand bolts of colored silks.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官判陝東道行台僕射，復從太宗討王世充。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, while retaining his original office, he served as acting Vice Director of the Shandong Circuit Directorate and again followed Taizong in campaigning against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting vice director of the Shandong Circuit directorate while retaining his original rank, and again followed Taizong against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 時通有二子並在洛陽，高祖謂通曰：「東征之事，今以相屬，其如兩子何？」

translations.literal: At the time Tutong had two sons both in Luoyang. Gaozu said to Tutong: "The eastern campaign is now entrusted to you—what of your two sons?"
translations.idiomatic: Tutong had two sons in Luoyang at the time. Gaozu said: "The eastern campaign is now in your hands—what of your two sons?"

sentences.zh: 通對曰：「臣以老朽，誠不足以當重任。

translations.literal: Tutong replied: "Your servant is old and worn and truly unfit for a weighty charge.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong replied: "I am old and worn and truly unfit for so weighty a charge.

sentences.zh: 但自惟疇昔，執就軍門，至尊釋其縲囚，加之恩禮，既不能死，實荷再生。

translations.literal: Yet reflecting on the past, I came of my own accord to the army gate; Your Majesty released me from bonds and added favor and ceremony—having failed to die, I truly owe a second life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I recall the past, I came of my own accord to your army gate. Your Majesty released me from bonds and treated me with grace and ceremony. Having failed to die then, I owe you a second life.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，心口相誓，暗以身命奉許國家久矣。

translations.literal: At that time heart and mouth swore together; in secret I pledged my person and life to the state long ago.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment heart and mouth swore as one: in secret I pledged my life to the state long ago.

sentences.zh: 今此行臣願先驅，兩兒若死，自是其命，終不以私害義。」

translations.literal: On this campaign your servant wishes to ride in the vanguard; if my two sons should die, that is their fate—I will never let private feeling harm public duty."
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign I wish to ride in the vanguard. If my two sons should die, that is their fate—I will never let private feeling harm public duty."

sentences.zh: 高祖嘆息曰：「徇義之夫，一至於此！」

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed and said: "A man who devotes himself to righteousness—to this degree!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed and said: "A man who devotes himself to righteousness—to this degree!"

sentences.zh: 及大兵圍洛陽，竇建德且至，太宗中分麾下以屬通，令與齊王元吉圍守洛陽。

translations.literal: When the great army besieged Luoyang and Dou Jiande was about to arrive, Taizong divided his forces in half and assigned them to Tutong, ordering him together with Prince of Qi Yuanji to besiege and hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army besieged Luoyang and Dou Jiande was approaching, Taizong divided his forces and gave half to Tutong, ordering him and the Prince of Qi, Yuanji, to hold the siege of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 世充平，通功為第一，尋拜陝東大行台右僕射，鎮於洛陽。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, Tutong's merit ranked first; shortly thereafter he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Great Shandong Circuit Directorate and garrisoned at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong fell, Tutong's merit ranked first. He was soon appointed right vice director of the great Shandong Circuit directorate and garrisoned at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，征拜刑部尚書，通自以不習文法，固辭之，轉工部尚書。

translations.literal: After several years he was summoned as Minister of Punishments; Tutong, considering himself unversed in legal statutes, firmly declined and was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was summoned as minister of punishments. Tutong, considering himself unversed in legal statutes, firmly declined and was made minister of works instead.

sentences.zh: 隱太子之誅也，通復檢校行台僕射，馳鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: At the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince, Tutong was again made acting Vice Director of the Circuit Directorate and galloped to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince was killed, Tutong was again made acting vice director of the circuit directorate and galloped to garrison Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，行台廢，授洛州都督，賜實封六百戶，加左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the circuit directorate was abolished; he was appointed Military Governor of Luo Province, granted six hundred households of substantive fief, and given the additional title of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan the circuit directorate was abolished. He was appointed military governor of Luo Province, granted a substantive fief of six hundred households, and given the additional title of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 太宗痛惜久之，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Taizong grieved for him long; he was posthumously given the post of Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong grieved for him a long while. He was posthumously made right vice director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子壽襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸洛陽宮，思通忠節，拜其少子詮果毅都尉，賜束帛以恤其家焉。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited the Luoyang Palace, thinking of Tutong's loyalty and integrity, he appointed his younger son Quan Colonel of Valor and Courage and bestowed bolts of silk to comfort his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong visited the Luoyang Palace and thought of Tutong's loyalty, he appointed his younger son Quan colonel of valor and courage and bestowed bolts of silk to comfort the family.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔圖形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered his portrait painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered his portrait painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，與房玄齡配饗太宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was paired with Fang Xuanling for sacrifice in Taizong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was paired with Fang Xuanling for sacrifice in Taizong's temple court.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，重贈司空。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again posthumously given the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 詮官至瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Quan rose to the post of Inspector of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quan rose to inspector of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詮子仲翔，神龍中亦為瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Quan's son Zhongxiang, during the Shenlong era, also served as Inspector of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's son Zhongxiang also served as inspector of Ying Prefecture during the Shenlong era.

sentences.zh: 任瑰，字瑋，廬州合肥人，陳鎮東大將軍蠻奴弟之子也。

translations.literal: Ren Gui, styled Wei, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou, the son of the younger brother of Manu, the Chen Eastern Garrison Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui, styled Wei, came from Hefei in Luzhou. He was the son of the younger brother of Manu, Chen's grand general of the eastern garrison.

sentences.zh: 父七寶，仕陳定遠太守。

translations.literal: His father Qibao served Chen as Administrator of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qibao had served Chen as administrator of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑰早孤，蠻奴愛之，情逾己子，每稱曰：「吾子侄雖多，並傭保耳，門戶所寄，惟在於瑰。」

translations.literal: Gui was orphaned early; Manu loved him with affection surpassing his own sons, and often said: "Though I have many sons and nephews, they are all hired hands—the hope of the house rests on Gui alone."
translations.idiomatic: Gui was orphaned young. Manu loved him more than his own sons and often said: "I have many sons and nephews, but they are all hired hands—the hope of our house rests on Gui alone."

sentences.zh: 年十九，試守靈溪令。

translations.literal: At nineteen he was appointed on trial as magistrate of Lingxi.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he was appointed on trial as magistrate of Lingxi.

sentences.zh: 俄遷衡州司馬，都督王勇甚敬異之，委以州府之務。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Vice Governor of Heng Prefecture; the Military Governor Wang Yong greatly respected and admired him and entrusted him with the affairs of the prefecture and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice governor of Heng Prefecture. Military Governor Wang Yong greatly respected him and entrusted him with the affairs of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬隋師滅陳，瑰勸勇據嶺南，求陳氏子孫立以為帝；

translations.literal: When Sui forces destroyed Chen, Gui urged Yong to hold the Lingnan region, seek out a descendant of the Chen house, and set him up as emperor;
translations.idiomatic: When Sui forces destroyed Chen, Gui urged Yong to hold Lingnan, find a descendant of the Chen house, and set him up as emperor;

sentences.zh: 勇不能用，以嶺外降隋，瑰乃棄官而去。

translations.literal: Yong could not adopt the plan and surrendered the region beyond the mountains to Sui; Gui thereupon resigned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yong would not listen and surrendered the region beyond the mountains to Sui. Gui resigned his office and left.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，為韓城尉，俄又罷職。

translations.literal: During Renshou he served as Assistant Magistrate of Hancheng, but shortly thereafter was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou he served as assistant magistrate of Hancheng, but was soon dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 及高祖討捕於汾、晉，瑰謁高祖於轅門，承製為河東縣戶曹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was campaigning in Fen and Jin, Gui presented himself at the army gate and received an imperial order appointing him Registrar of Households for Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was campaigning in Fen and Jin, Gui presented himself at the army gate and was appointed registrar of households for Hedong County by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 高祖將之晉陽，留隱太子建成以托於瑰。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was about to go to Jinyang, he left the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng in Gui's care.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was about to go to Jinyang, he left the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng in Gui's care.

sentences.zh: 義師起，瑰至龍門謁見。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Gui went to Longmen to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Gui went to Longmen to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「隋氏失馭，天下沸騰。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him: "The Sui house has lost the reins; the realm seethes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said to him: "The Sui house has lost the reins, and the realm seethes.

sentences.zh: 吾忝以外戚，屬當重寄，不可坐觀時變。

translations.literal: I am shamed to be an affinal relative of the throne and bear a weighty charge—I cannot sit and watch the times change.
translations.idiomatic: As an affinal relative of the throne I bear a weighty charge—I cannot sit idle while the times change.

sentences.zh: 晉陽是用武之地，士馬精強，今率驍雄以匡國難。

translations.literal: Jinyang is a place for wielding military force; troops and horses are elite and strong—now I lead the valiant and heroic to set right the state's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang is a place made for war; our troops and horses are strong. Now I lead the brave to set right the state's peril.

sentences.zh: 卿將家子，深有智謀，觀吾此舉，將為濟否？」

translations.literal: You are a general's son, deep in wisdom and stratagem—looking at this move of mine, will it succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a general's son, deep in wisdom and stratagem—do you think this venture of mine will succeed?"

sentences.zh: 瑰曰：「後主殘酷無道，征役不息，天下恟恟，思聞拯亂。

translations.literal: Gui said: "The Later Sovereign is cruel and without the Way; corvée labor never ceases; the realm clamors, longing to hear of deliverance from chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said: "The Later Sovereign is cruel and without the Way. Corvée labor never ceases. The realm clamors for deliverance from chaos.

sentences.zh: 公天縱神武，親舉義師，所下城邑，秋毫無犯，軍令嚴明，將士用命。

translations.literal: Your Lordship is heaven-endowed with divine martial prowess, personally raising the righteous army; the cities you take suffer not the slightest harm, military orders are strict and clear, and officers and men obey commands.
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship is heaven-endowed with divine martial prowess and have personally raised the righteous army. The cities you take suffer not the slightest harm. Your military orders are strict and clear, and your officers and men obey without fail.

sentences.zh: 關中所在蜂起，惟待義兵。

translations.literal: Throughout Guanzhong, [uprisings] spring up everywhere like swarming bees; they only await the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Guanzhong, uprisings are springing up everywhere like swarming bees, and they are only waiting for a righteous army.

sentences.zh: 仗大順，從眾欲，何憂不濟？

translations.literal: Relying on the Great Mandate and following the people's desires, why worry that success will not be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: If you rely on the Great Mandate and follow the people's desires, why should you worry that you will not succeed?

sentences.zh: 瑰在馮翊積年，人情諳練，願為一介之使，銜命入關，同州已東，必當款伏。

translations.literal: Gui has accumulated years in Fengyi and is thoroughly versed in local sentiment; I wish to serve as a lone envoy, bearing orders to enter the Pass—east of Tongzhou, all will surely submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: I have spent many years in Fengyi and know the local sentiment well. I wish to serve as a lone envoy and enter the Pass on your orders; east of Tongzhou, the people will surely submit in good faith.

sentences.zh: 於梁山船濟，直指韓城，進逼合陽，分取朝邑。

translations.literal: Cross by boat at Liangshan, strike directly at Hancheng, advance to press Heyang, and detach forces to take Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Cross the river by boat at Liangshan, strike straight at Hancheng, advance to threaten Heyang, and detach troops to seize Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 且蕭造文吏，本無武略，仰懼威靈，理當自下；

translations.literal: Moreover, Xiao Zao is a civil official and originally has no military strategy; awed by your authority and prestige, by right he ought to submit of his own accord;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Xiao Zao is a civil official with no real military skill. Awed by your authority and prestige, he ought by rights to submit of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 孫華諸賊，未有適從，必當相率而至。

translations.literal: Sun Hua and the other bandits, having no proper master to follow, will surely come leading one another in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hua and the other bandits have no proper leader to follow and will surely come over to you in a body.

sentences.zh: 然後鼓行整眾，入據永豐，雖未得京城，關中固已定矣。」

translations.literal: Then, advancing with drums beating and ranks in order, enter and hold Yongfeng; though the capital may not yet be taken, Guanzhong will surely be secured."
translations.idiomatic: Then advance with drums beating and ranks in order, enter and hold Yongfeng. Even if the capital is not yet taken, Guanzhong will already be secured."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「是吾心也。」

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said: "That is exactly what I have in mind."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Gaozu said, "That is exactly what I have in mind."

sentences.zh: 乃授銀青光祿大夫，遣陳演壽、史大奈領步騎六千，趨梁山渡河，使瑰及薛獻為招慰大使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed [Gui as] Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, dispatched Chen Yanshou and Shi Dana to lead six thousand infantry and cavalry, hastening to Liangshan to cross the river, and made Gui and Xue Xian pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he appointed Gui Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, dispatched Chen Yanshou and Shi Dana at the head of six thousand infantry and cavalry to hurry to Liangshan and cross the river, and made Gui and Xue Xian pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂演壽曰：「閫外之事，宜與任瑰籌之。」

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said to Yanshou: "Matters outside the gate should be planned together with Ren Gui."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Gaozu told Yanshou, "On military matters beyond the capital, you should plan together with Ren Gui."

sentences.zh: 孫華、白玄度等聞兵且至，果競來降，並具舟於河，師遂利涉。

translations.literal: Sun Hua, Bai Xuandu, and the others, hearing that troops were about to arrive, indeed competed to come and surrender; they also prepared boats on the river, and the army crossed with ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hua, Bai Xuandu, and the others heard that the army was approaching, they indeed vied to come and surrender. They also prepared boats on the river, and the army crossed without difficulty.

sentences.zh: 瑰說下韓城縣，與諸將進擊飲馬泉，破之，拜左光祿大夫，留守永豐倉。

translations.literal: Gui persuaded Hancheng County to submit; together with the generals he advanced to attack Yinma Spring and defeated it; he was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and left behind to guard Yongfeng Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Gui persuaded Hancheng County to submit, then joined the other generals in an advance against Yinma Spring and defeated it. He was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and left behind to guard Yongfeng Granary.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，改授谷州刺史。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, [Gui] was reassigned as Prefect of Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Gui was reassigned as prefect of Guzhou.

sentences.zh: 王世充數率眾攻新安，瑰拒戰破之，以功累封管國公。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong repeatedly led armies to attack Xin'an; Gui resisted in battle and defeated him; for his merits he was repeatedly ennobled until made Duke of Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong repeatedly led armies to attack Xin'an, but Gui fought him off and defeated him. For his achievements he was repeatedly ennobled until he was made Duke of Gu.

sentences.zh: 太宗率師討世充，瑰從至邙山，使檢校水運以供餉饋。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizong led troops to campaign against Shichong; Gui followed him to Mount Mang and was made to inspect water transport to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong led an army against Shichong, Gui accompanied him to Mount Mang and was put in charge of inspecting water transport to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 關東初定，持節為河南道安撫大使。

translations.literal: When the eastern pass region was first pacified, [he] held the imperial tally as Pacification Commissioner of Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern pass region was first pacified, he was given the imperial tally and appointed Pacification Commissioner of Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 世充弟辯為徐州行台尚書令，率所部詣瑰降。

translations.literal: Shichong's younger brother Bian, who was Executive Director of the Xuzhou Regional Headquarters, led his forces to Gui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's younger brother Bian, who served as executive director of the Xuzhou regional headquarters, led his troops to Gui and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 瑰至宋州，屬徐圓朗據兗州反，曹、戴諸州咸應之。

translations.literal: When Gui reached Songzhou, Xu Yuanlang held Yanzhou in rebellion, and the prefectures of Cao, Dai, and others all responded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui reached Songzhou, Xu Yuanlang had seized Yanzhou and rebelled, and the prefectures of Cao, Dai, and others all rose in support.

sentences.zh: 副使柳浚勸瑰退保汴州，瑰笑曰：「柳公何怯也！

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Liu Jun urged Gui to withdraw and hold Bianzhou; Gui laughed and said: "Master Liu, how timid you are!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Liu Jun urged Gui to fall back and hold Bianzhou. Gui laughed and said, "Master Liu, how timid you are!

sentences.zh: 老將居邊甚久，自當有計，非公所知。」

translations.literal: This old general has long been stationed on the frontier; I naturally have a plan—it is not for you to know."
translations.idiomatic: This old general has been on the frontier a long time and naturally has a plan of his own. That is not for you to know."

sentences.zh: 圓朗俄又攻陷楚丘，引兵將圍虞城，瑰遣崔樞、張公謹自鄢陵領諸州豪右質子百餘人守虞城以拒賊。

translations.literal: Yuanlang soon also captured Chuqiu and was about to lead troops to besiege Yucheng; Gui dispatched Cui Shu and Zhang Gongjin from Yanling to lead over a hundred hostages—the sons of local elites from various prefectures—to defend Yucheng against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang soon captured Chuqiu as well and was about to lead his army to besiege Yucheng. Gui dispatched Cui Shu and Zhang Gongjin from Yanling at the head of more than a hundred hostages, sons of local elites from the various prefectures, to hold Yucheng against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 浚又諫曰：「樞與公謹並世充之將，又諸州質子父兄皆反，此必為變。」

translations.literal: Jun again remonstrated: "Shu and Gongjin were both Shichong's generals, and the fathers and elder brothers of the hostages from the prefectures have all rebelled—this will surely turn into treachery."
translations.idiomatic: Jun remonstrated again, "Shu and Gongjin were both Shichong's generals, and the fathers and elder brothers of the hostages from the prefectures have all rebelled. This is bound to end in treachery."

sentences.zh: 瑰不答。

translations.literal: Gui did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gui made no reply.

sentences.zh: 樞至，則分配質子，並與土人合隊居守。

translations.literal: When Shu arrived, he distributed the hostages and mixed them with local men in combined squads to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu arrived, he distributed the hostages and mixed them with local men in combined squads to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 賊既稍近，質子有叛者，樞因斬其隊帥。

translations.literal: As the rebels drew nearer, some hostages tried to defect; Shu thereupon executed their squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels drew nearer, some of the hostages tried to defect, so Shu executed their squad leader.

sentences.zh: 城中人懼曰：「質子父兄悉來為賊，賊之子弟安可守城？」

translations.literal: The people in the city feared and said: "The hostages' fathers and elder brothers have all come as rebels—how can the rebels' sons and younger brothers be trusted to hold the city?"
translations.idiomatic: The people in the city grew afraid and said, "The hostages' fathers and elder brothers have all come as rebels. How can the rebels' sons and younger brothers be trusted to hold the city?"

sentences.zh: 樞因縱諸隊各殺質子，梟首於門外，遣使報瑰。

translations.literal: Shu then allowed each squad to kill its hostages, displayed the heads outside the gate, and sent a messenger to report to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Shu then let each squad kill its hostages, displayed the heads outside the gate, and sent a messenger to report to Gui.

sentences.zh: 瑰陽怒曰：「遣將去者，欲招慰耳，何罪而殺之？」

translations.literal: Gui feigned anger and said: "I sent that general there to win people over through conciliation—what crime had they committed that they should be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui feigned anger and said, "I sent that general there to win people over peacefully. What crime had they committed that they should be killed?"

sentences.zh: 退謂浚曰：「固知崔樞辦之。

translations.literal: Privately he said to Jun: "I knew all along that Cui Shu would handle it this way.
translations.idiomatic: In private he said to Jun, "I knew all along that Cui Shu would handle it this way.

sentences.zh: 既遣縣人殺賊質子，冤隙已大，吾何患焉？」

translations.literal: Since he had the county men kill the rebels' hostages, the grievance between us and the enemy is already great—what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has had the county men kill the rebels' hostages, the enmity between us and the enemy is already deep. What do I have to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 樞果拒卻圓朗。

translations.literal: Shu indeed repulsed Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did indeed repulse Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷徐州總管，仍為大使。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, [Gui] was transferred to be Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou, still serving as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Gui was transferred to commander-in-chief of Xuzhou while continuing to serve as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瑰選補官吏，頗私親故，或依倚其勢，多所求納，瑰知而不禁；

translations.literal: When Gui selected and appointed officials, he favored relatives and old associates; some, relying on his power, made many demands and bribes; Gui knew but did not prohibit this;
translations.idiomatic: When Gui selected and appointed officials, he often favored relatives and old associates. Some, relying on his power, made many demands and took bribes, and Gui knew of it but did not stop them.

sentences.zh: 又，妻劉氏妒悍無禮，為世所譏。

translations.literal: Moreover, his wife Lady Liu was jealous, fierce, and without propriety, and was ridiculed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his wife Lady Liu was jealous, overbearing, and lacking in propriety, and was widely ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 及輔公祏平，拜邢州都督。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi was pacified, [Gui] was appointed Military Governor of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi was pacified, Gui was appointed military governor of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隱太子之誅也，瑰弟璨，時為典膳監，瑰坐左遷通州都督。

translations.literal: At the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince, Gui's younger brother Can was at the time Director of Palace Commissary; Gui was implicated and demoted to Military Governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince, Gui's younger brother Can was serving as director of palace commissary. Gui was implicated and demoted to military governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 丘和，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Qiu He was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父壽，魏鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shou was Eastern Pacifying General under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shou had served as Eastern Pacifying General under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 和少便弓馬，重氣任俠。

translations.literal: He from youth was adept with bow and horse, valued bold spirit, and lived as a knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was skilled with bow and horse, prized bold spirit, and lived as a knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 及長，始折節，與物無忤，無貴賤皆愛之。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he first restrained his ways; with others he had no conflict; without distinction of high or low, all loved him.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older, he first learned to restrain himself. He got along with everyone, and people of every rank loved him.

sentences.zh: 周為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou he was made Opening the Government, Grand Master with the Same Title as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Zhou he was made Opening the Government, Grand Master with the Same Title as the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 入隋，累遷右武衛將軍，封平城郡公。

translations.literal: Entering the Sui, he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui came to power, he rose through repeated promotions to general of the Right Martial Guard and was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之反也，以和為蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, [He] was made Prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Qiu He was appointed prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 諒使兵士服婦人服，戴冪旂，奄至城中，和脫身而免，由是除名。

translations.literal: Liang had soldiers dress in women's clothing and wear veiled head cloths; they suddenly arrived in the city; He escaped with his life and was thereby dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had his soldiers dress in women's clothing and wear veiled head cloths, then suddenly entered the city. He escaped with his life and was dismissed from office as a result.

sentences.zh: 時宇文述方被任遇，和傾心附之，又以發武陵公元胄罪，拜代州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Shu was just then being trusted and favored; He devoted himself and attached to him; also because he exposed the crimes of Prince of Wuling Yuan Zhou, he was appointed Prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuwen Shu was enjoying great favor at court, and He devoted himself to him. He also won appointment as prefect of Daizhou by exposing the crimes of Yuan Zhou, Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 屬煬帝北巡過代州，和獻食甚精，及至朔州，刺史楊廓獨無所獻，帝不悅，而宇文述又盛稱之，乃以和為博陵太守，仍令楊廓至博陵觀和為式。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang on his northern tour passed through Daizhou, He presented food of exceptional refinement; when [the emperor] reached Shuozhou, Prefect Yang Kuo alone presented nothing, and the emperor was displeased; moreover Yuwen Shu lavishly praised [He], so [the emperor] made He Prefect of Boling and also ordered Yang Kuo to go to Boling and observe He's methods as a model.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang passed through Daizhou on his northern tour, He presented food of exceptional refinement. When the emperor reached Shuozhou, Prefect Yang Kuo alone presented nothing, and the emperor was displeased. Yuwen Shu then lavishly praised He, so the emperor made He prefect of Boling and ordered Yang Kuo to go to Boling and observe He's methods as a model.

sentences.zh: 及駕至博陵，和上食又豐，帝益稱之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Boling, He's presentation of food was again abundant, and the emperor praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Boling, He's presentation of food was again lavish, and the emperor praised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 由是所幸處獻食者競為華侈。

translations.literal: From this, those who presented food at places favored by the emperor competed in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, officials at every place the emperor favored competed to present food in ever more lavish style.

sentences.zh: 和在郡善撫吏士，甚得歡心，尋遷天水郡守。

translations.literal: He in the commandery treated officials and soldiers well and won great goodwill; soon he was transferred to be Administrator of Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery He treated officials and soldiers well and won great goodwill. Soon he was transferred to administrator of Tianshui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大業末，以海南僻遠，吏多侵漁，百姓咸怨，數為亂逆，於是選淳良太守以撫之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, because Hainan was remote and distant, officials often exploited and plundered, the common people all resented it, and disturbances repeatedly broke out; thereupon they selected upright and good prefects to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, the region south of the sea was remote and officials there often exploited the people. The common people resented this bitterly and repeatedly rose in rebellion, so the court chose upright and capable prefects to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎裴矩奏言：「丘和歷居二郡，皆以惠政著聞，寬而不擾。」

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Ju memorialized, saying: "Qiu He has successively governed two commanderies, in each case becoming renowned for benevolent administration, lenient and without harassment."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Ju memorialized, saying, "Qiu He has governed two commanderies in succession and in each has become renowned for benevolent rule that is lenient and free of harassment."

sentences.zh: 煬帝從之，遣和為交趾太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang followed this advice and dispatched He as Prefect of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang accepted this and dispatched He as prefect of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 既至，撫諸豪傑，甚得蠻夷之心。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he pacified the local magnates and won the hearts of the barbarian peoples exceedingly well.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he won over the local magnates and gained the deep loyalty of the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 會煬帝為化及所弒，鴻臚卿寧長真以鬱林、始安之地附於蕭銑；

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Yang was assassinated by Huaji; Grand Master of Ceremonial Ning Changzhen submitted the territories of Yulin and Shian to Xiao Xian;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was assassinated by Yuwen Huaji, Grand Master of Ceremonial Ning Changzhen submitted the territories of Yulin and Shian to Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 馮盎以蒼梧、高涼、珠崖、番禺之地附於林士弘。

translations.literal: Feng Ang submitted the territories of Cangwu, Gaoliang, Zhuya, and Panyu to Lin Shihong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang submitted the territories of Cangwu, Gaoliang, Zhuya, and Panyu to Lin Shihong.

sentences.zh: 各遣人召之，和初未知隋亡，皆不就。

translations.literal: Each dispatched men to summon him; He at first did not yet know the Sui had fallen and did not go to either.
translations.idiomatic: Each sent envoys to summon him, but He did not yet know the Sui had fallen and refused both.

sentences.zh: 林邑之西諸國，並遣遺和明珠、文犀、金寶之物，富埒王者。

translations.literal: The various states west of Linyi all sent He pearls, patterned rhinoceros horn, and gold and treasure, making him as wealthy as a king.
translations.idiomatic: The various states west of Linyi all sent him pearls, patterned rhinoceros horn, and gold and treasure, until his wealth rivaled that of a king.

sentences.zh: 銑利之，遣長真率百越之眾渡海侵和，和遣高士廉率交、愛首領擊之，長真退走，境內獲全，郡中樹碑頌德。

translations.literal: Xian coveted this and dispatched Changzhen to lead the Baiyue peoples across the sea to invade He; He dispatched Gao Shilian to lead the chieftains of Jiao and Ai to attack them; Changzhen retreated and fled, the territory within the borders was preserved intact, and the commandery erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian coveted this wealth and dispatched Changzhen at the head of the Baiyue peoples across the sea to invade He. He sent Gao Shilian at the head of the chieftains of Jiao and Ai to attack them. Changzhen retreated, the territory was preserved intact, and the commandery erected a stele in praise of He's virtue.

sentences.zh: 會舊驍果從江都還者，審知隋滅，遂以州從銑。

translations.literal: It happened that veterans of the Xiaoguo Guard returning from Jiangdu learned that the Sui had perished and thereupon submitted the prefecture to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When veterans of the Xiaoguo Guard returning from Jiangdu learned that the Sui had fallen, they submitted the prefecture to Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 及銑平，和以海南之地歸國。

translations.literal: When Xian was pacified, He returned the lands south of the sea to the [Tang] state.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian was defeated, He returned the lands south of the sea to the Tang state.

sentences.zh: 詔使李道裕即授上柱國、譚國公、交州總管。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Li Daoyu to invest him on the spot as Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Tan, and Commander-in-Chief of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Li Daoyu to invest him on the spot as supreme pillar of the state, Duke of Tan, and commander-in-chief of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 和遣司馬高士廉奉表請入朝，詔許之。

translations.literal: He dispatched his aide Gao Shilian to present a memorial requesting permission to come to court; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his aide Gao Shilian to present a memorial requesting permission to come to court, and the edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣其子師利迎之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor dispatched his son Shili to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu dispatched his son Shili to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，高祖為之興，引入臥內，語及平生，甚歡，奏《九部樂》以饗之，拜左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: When he had an audience, the High Ancestor rose for him, brought him into the inner chamber, spoke of their lives together with great pleasure, had the Nine Section Music performed to feast him, and appointed him General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience, Emperor Gaozu rose to receive him, brought him into the inner chamber, and talked of their lives together with great pleasure. The Nine Section Music was performed in his honor, and he was appointed general-in-chief of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 和時年已衰老，乃拜稷州刺史，以是本鄉，令自怡養。

translations.literal: He was by then already aged and infirm, so [the emperor] appointed him Prefect of Jizhou; because it was his native place, he was allowed to nourish himself in ease.
translations.idiomatic: By then He was already old and frail, so he was appointed prefect of Jizhou. Because it was his native place, he was allowed to live there in comfort and ease.

sentences.zh: 九年，除特進。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made special advancement.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year of Zhenguan, at the age of eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of the Zhenguan era, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈荊州總管，謚曰襄，賜東園秘器，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou; his posthumous title was Xiang; he was granted Eastern Garden funerary regalia and buried with honor at Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made commander-in-chief of Jingzhou, given the posthumous title Xiang, granted Eastern Garden funerary regalia, and buried with honor at Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 有子十五人，多至大官，惟行恭知名。

translations.literal: He had fifteen sons, most of whom reached high office; only Xinggong became widely known.
translations.idiomatic: He had fifteen sons, most of whom reached high office, but only Xinggong became widely known.

sentences.zh: 行恭善騎射，勇敢絕倫。

translations.literal: Xinggong was skilled in mounted archery and in courage was without peer.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong was skilled in mounted archery and was unmatched in courage.

sentences.zh: 大業末，與兄師利聚兵於岐、雍間。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, together with his elder brother Shili he gathered troops between Qi and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, he and his elder brother Shili gathered troops in the region between Qi and Yong.

sentences.zh: 有眾一萬，保故郿城，百姓多附之，群盜不敢入境。

translations.literal: He had ten thousand followers, held the old city of Mei, many common people attached themselves to him, and bandit gangs did not dare enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten thousand followers, held the old city of Mei, and many common people rallied to him, so bandit gangs did not dare enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 初，原州奴賊數萬人圍扶風，郡太守竇璡堅守，經數月，賊中食盡，野無所掠，眾多離散，投行恭者千餘騎。

translations.literal: Earlier, slave rebels from Yuanzhou numbering in the tens of thousands besieged Fufeng; the commandery administrator Dou Qin held firm; after several months the rebels' food was exhausted and there was nothing left to plunder in the countryside; many dispersed, and more than a thousand horsemen came to join Xinggong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, tens of thousands of slave rebels from Yuanzhou had besieged Fufeng. The commandery administrator Dou Qin held firm for several months until the rebels' food ran out and there was nothing left to plunder in the countryside. Many dispersed, and more than a thousand horsemen came over to Xinggong.

sentences.zh: 行恭遣其酋渠說諸奴賊共迎義軍。

translations.literal: Xinggong dispatched their chieftains to persuade the slave rebels together to welcome the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong sent their chieftains to persuade the slave rebels to welcome the righteous army together.

sentences.zh: 行恭又率五百人，皆負米麥，持牛酒，自詣賊營。

translations.literal: Xinggong also led five hundred men, all carrying rice and wheat on their backs and bearing cattle and wine, and went in person to the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong then led five hundred men, all carrying rice and wheat on their backs and bearing cattle and wine, and went in person to the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 奴帥長揖，行恭手斬之，謂其眾曰：「汝等並是好人，何因事奴為主，使天下號為奴賊？」

translations.literal: The slave leader gave a long bow; Xinggong personally cut him down with his hand and said to the crowd: "You are all good men—why serve a slave as master and let the realm call you slave rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: The slave leader bowed deeply. Xinggong cut him down with his own hand and said to the crowd, "You are all good men. Why serve a slave as your master and let the whole realm call you slave rebels?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆俯伏曰：「願改事公。」

translations.literal: The crowd all prostrated themselves and said: "We wish to serve you instead."
translations.idiomatic: The whole crowd prostrated themselves and said, "We wish to serve you instead."

sentences.zh: 行恭率其眾與師利共謁太宗於渭北，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Xinggong led his followers together with Shili to have an audience with the Emperor Taizong north of the Wei River and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong led his followers and Shili together to have an audience with Emperor Taizong north of the Wei River, and he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從平京城，討薛舉、劉武周、王世充、竇建德，皆立殊勳，授左一府驃騎，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of the capital, and in campaigns against Xue Ju, Liu Wuzhou, Wang Shichong, and Dou Jiande he each time achieved outstanding merit; he was appointed Flying Cavalry General of the Left First Office and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of the capital and in campaigns against Xue Ju, Liu Wuzhou, Wang Shichong, and Dou Jiande, distinguishing himself in each. He was appointed Flying Cavalry General of the Left First Office and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 隱太子之誅也，行恭以功遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince, Xinggong was transferred to General of the Left Guard for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince, Xinggong was transferred to general of the Left Guard for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，坐與嫡兄爭葬所生母，為法司所劾，除名。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, he was implicated for disputing with his elder brother of the principal line over the burial of their birth mother, was impeached by the legal authorities, and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, he was impeached and dismissed from office for disputing with his elder brother of the principal line over the burial of their birth mother.

sentences.zh: 因從侯君集平高昌，封天水郡公，累除右武候將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Hou Junji in pacifying Gaochang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and was repeatedly appointed General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Hou Junji in pacifying Gaochang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and was repeatedly appointed general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，歷遷右武侯大將軍、冀陝二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, [Xinggong] was repeatedly transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard and Prefect of the two prefectures of Ji and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he rose through repeated appointments to general-in-chief of the Right Martial Guard and prefect of Ji and Shan.

sentences.zh: 尋請致仕，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he requested retirement and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he requested retirement and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Longde, at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Longde era, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈荊州都督，謚曰襄，賜溫明秘器，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Protector-General of Jingzhou; his posthumous title was Xiang; he was granted Warm Bright funerary regalia and buried with honor at Zhao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made protector-general of Jingzhou, given the posthumous title Xiang, granted Warm Bright funerary regalia, and buried with honor at Zhao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 行恭性嚴酷，所在僚列皆懾憚之，數坐事解免。

translations.literal: Xinggong was by nature severe and harsh; wherever he served, his subordinates all feared him, and he was repeatedly dismissed from office for various offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong was severe and harsh by nature. Wherever he served, his subordinates feared him, and he was repeatedly dismissed from office for various offenses.

sentences.zh: 太宗每思其功，不逾時月復其官。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizong, each time mindful of his achievements, restored him to office within no more than a month or two.
translations.idiomatic: Each time, Emperor Taizong, mindful of his achievements, restored him to office within a month or two.

sentences.zh: 初，從討王世充，會戰於邙山之上。

translations.literal: Earlier, when he followed the campaign against Wang Shichong, they joined battle on Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when he followed the campaign against Wang Shichong, they joined battle on Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲知其虛實強弱，乃與數十騎沖之，直出其後，眾皆披靡，莫敢當其鋒，所殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizong wished to know the enemy's true strength and weakness; thereupon with several dozen horsemen he charged them, bursting straight out behind them; the enemy all collapsed before him, none dared meet his spearhead, and those killed and wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong wished to test the enemy's true strength, so with several dozen horsemen he charged straight through to their rear. The enemy collapsed before him, none dared meet his spearhead, and he killed and wounded a great many.

sentences.zh: 既而限以長堤，與諸騎相失，惟行恭獨從。

translations.literal: Soon he was hemmed in by a long embankment, became separated from the other horsemen, and only Xinggong followed alone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was hemmed in by a long embankment and became separated from the other horsemen. Only Xinggong remained with him.

sentences.zh: 尋有勁騎數人追及太宗，矢中御馬；

translations.literal: Before long several fierce horsemen caught up with the Emperor Taizong, and arrows struck the imperial horse;
translations.idiomatic: Before long several fierce horsemen caught up with Emperor Taizong, and arrows struck his horse.

sentences.zh: 行恭乃回騎射之，發無不中，餘賊不敢復前。

translations.literal: Xinggong thereupon wheeled his horse and shot at them; every shot hit, and the remaining rebels did not dare advance again.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong wheeled his horse and shot at them. Every shot hit its mark, and the remaining rebels did not dare advance again.

sentences.zh: 然後下馬拔箭，以其所乘馬進太宗。

translations.literal: Then he dismounted, pulled out the arrows, and presented his own horse to the Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Then he dismounted, pulled out the arrows, and gave his own horse to Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 行恭於御馬前步執長刀，巨躍大呼，斬數人，突陣而出，得入大軍。

translations.literal: Xinggong walked before the imperial horse holding a long saber, leaping greatly and shouting loudly; he cut down several men, burst through the enemy formation, and was able to rejoin the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong walked ahead of the imperial horse with a long saber in hand, leaping and shouting. He cut down several men, burst through the enemy formation, and rejoined the main army.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，有詔刻石為人馬以象行恭拔箭之狀，立於昭陵闕前。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, there was an edict to carve stone figures of men and horses depicting Xinggong pulling out the arrows, and to set them up before the gate-towers of Zhao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era, an edict ordered stone figures of men and horses carved to depict Xinggong pulling out the arrows, and they were set up before the gate-towers of Zhao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 和少子行掩，高宗時為少府監。

translations.literal: He's youngest son Xingyan, during Gaozong's reign, was Supervisor of the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: He's youngest son Xingyan served as supervisor of the palace workshop under Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 許紹，字嗣宗，本高陽人也，梁末徙於周，因家於安陸。

translations.literal: Xu Shao, courtesy name Sizong, was originally a native of Gaoyang; at the end of the Liang he moved to Zhou and thereafter made his home at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao, courtesy name Sizong, was originally from Gaoyang. At the end of the Liang dynasty his family moved to Zhou territory and settled at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 祖弘，父法光，俱為楚州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hong and his father Faguang both served as Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hong and his father Faguang had both served as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝為安州總管，故紹兒童時得與高祖同學，特相友愛。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang was Grand Commander of An Prefecture, Shao in his childhood was able to study together with Gaozu, and they were especially close friends.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Emperor Gaozu served as grand commander of An Prefecture, Shao studied alongside him as a boy, and the two became especially close.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為夷陵郡通守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, he served as Assistant Prefect of Yiling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign, he was appointed assistant prefect of Yiling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時盜賊競起，紹保全郡境，流戶自歸者數十萬口，開倉賑給，甚得人心。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere in rivalry; Shao preserved the whole commandery territory. Displaced households who returned on their own numbered several hundred thousand mouths. He opened the granaries for relief and distribution, and won people's hearts greatly.
translations.idiomatic: As bandits rose across the land, Shao kept the entire commandery secure. Several hundred thousand displaced people returned of their own accord; he opened the granaries to feed them and won deep popular support.

sentences.zh: 及江都弒逆，紹率郡人大臨三日，仍以郡遙屬越王侗。

translations.literal: When the regicide at Jiangdu occurred, Shao led the people of the commandery in mourning for three days, and still submitted the commandery from afar to the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassination at Jiangdu took place, Shao led the commandery in three days of public mourning and continued to acknowledge the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong, as sovereign from afar.

sentences.zh: 王世充篡位，乃率黔安、武陵、澧陽等諸郡遣使歸國，授硤州刺史，封安陸郡公。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the throne, he then led Qian'an, Wuling, Liyang, and other commanderies to dispatch envoys and return to the [Tang] state. [Shao] was appointed Prefect of Xia Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Anlu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong seized the throne, Shao led Qian'an, Wuling, Liyang, and other commanderies to submit envoys to the Tang cause. He was made prefect of Xia Prefecture and created Duke of Anlu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖降敕書曰：「昔在子衿，同遊庠序，博士吳琰，其妻姓仇，追想此時，宛然心目，荏苒歲月，遂成累紀。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent down an imperial edict saying: "In old days when we wore the youth's sash, we studied together at the academy. Master of Letters Wu Yan—his wife's surname was Qiu. Recalling that time, it is vivid before my eyes and in my heart; the passing years have stretched into many years.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu issued an edict that read: "In our youth we studied together at the academy—Master Wu Yan, whose wife's surname was Qiu. When I think back to those days, they rise before me as if yesterday; yet the years have slipped away and become whole decades.

sentences.zh: 且在安州之日，公家乃蒞岳州；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the days at An Prefecture, your family came to Yue Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: When I was in An Prefecture, your family was posted to Yue Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 渡遼之時，伯裔又同戎旅。

translations.literal: At the time of crossing the Liao, Boyi was again in the same army.
translations.idiomatic: On the expedition against Liaodong, your elder brother Boyi and I served in the same army.

sentences.zh: 安危契闊，累葉同之，其間游處，觸事可想。

translations.literal: In safety and danger, in parting and reunion—generations of our families have shared this; the times we spent together, every touch of memory can be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Through safety and danger, through separation and reunion, our families have shared fate across generations—every memory of those days together still comes alive.

sentences.zh: 雖盧綰與劉邦同裡，吳質共曹丕接席，以今方古，何足稱焉！

translations.literal: Although Lu Wan and Liu Bang were from the same village, and Wu Zhi shared a seat with Cao Pi—in comparing the present with antiquity, what is there worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan and Liu Bang were village neighbors, and Wu Zhi sat at table with Cao Pi—yet compared with what you and I share, what are such old stories worth!

sentences.zh: 而公追硯席之舊歡，存通家之曩好，明鑑去就之理，洞識成敗之機。

translations.literal: Yet you recall the old joys of shared inkstone and mat, preserve the former friendship between our families, clearly discern the principle of choosing when to leave or stay, and thoroughly understand the key to success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: You have cherished our old fellowship at the writing desk, kept alive the bond between our families, judged clearly where loyalty lay, and understood precisely how fortunes would turn.

sentences.zh: 爰自荊門，馳心絳闕，綏懷士庶，糾合賓僚，踰越江山，遠申誠款。

translations.literal: Starting from Jingmen, your heart hastened to the Crimson Gate; you soothed and embraced officials and commoners, assembled guests and subordinates, crossed mountains and rivers, and from afar expressed sincere allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingmen you turned your heart toward the imperial capital, won over officials and commoners, gathered allies and retainers, crossed mountains and rivers, and pledged your loyalty from afar.

sentences.zh: 覽此忠至，彌以慰懷。」

translations.literal: Reading this utmost loyalty, I am all the more comforted in heart."
translations.idiomatic: Reading this proof of your devotion comforts me deeply."

sentences.zh: 及蕭銑將董景珍以長沙來降，命紹率兵應之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian's general Dong Jingzhen surrendered Changsha, [Gaozu] ordered Shao to lead troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian's general Dong Jingzhen surrendered Changsha, the emperor ordered Shao to march in support.

sentences.zh: 以破銑功，拜其子智仁為溫州刺史，委以招慰。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating Xiao, [Gaozu] appointed his son Zhiren Prefect of Wen Prefecture, entrusting him with winning over and comforting [the region].
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Xiao Xian, Gaozu appointed Shao's son Zhiren prefect of Wen Prefecture and charged him with pacification and recruitment.

sentences.zh: 時蕭銑遣其將楊道生圍硤州，紹縱兵擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Xian dispatched his general Yang Daosheng to besiege Xia Prefecture; Shao unleashed his troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian then sent his general Yang Daosheng to besiege Xia Prefecture, but Shao sallied forth and routed him.

sentences.zh: 銑又遣其將陳普環乘大艦溯江入硤，與開州賊蕭阇提規取巴蜀。

translations.literal: Xiao again sent his general Chen Puhuan to ride great warships upstream into the Xia Gorge, plotting with the Kai Prefecture rebel Xiao Dati to seize Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian next sent Chen Puhuan with large warships upriver into the Xia Gorge to join the Kai Prefecture rebel Xiao Dati in a bid to seize Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 紹遣智仁及錄事參軍李弘節、子婿張玄靜追至西陵硤，大破之，生擒普環，收其船艦。

translations.literal: Shao sent Zhiren, Record-Keeping Aide Li Hongjie, and his son-in-law Zhang Xuanjing in pursuit to Xiling Gorge, routed them completely, captured Puhuan alive, and seized their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Shao dispatched Zhiren, together with record-keeping aide Li Hongjie and his son-in-law Zhang Xuanjing, in pursuit to Xiling Gorge. They won a great victory, captured Chen Puhuan alive, and seized his fleet.

sentences.zh: 江南岸有安蜀城，與硤州相對，次東有荊門城，皆險峻，銑並以兵鎮守。

translations.literal: On the south bank of the river were Anshu Fortress, facing Xia Prefecture across the water, and farther east Jingmen Fortress—all steep and defensible. Xiao garrisoned them all with troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the south bank stood Anshu Fort, opposite Xia Prefecture, and farther east Jingmen Fort—both formidable strongpoints that Xiao Xian held with garrisons.

sentences.zh: 紹遣智仁及李弘節攻荊門鎮，破之。

translations.literal: Shao sent Zhiren and Li Hongjie to attack the Jingmen garrison and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Zhiren and Li Hongjie against the Jingmen garrison and took it.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，下制褒美，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased, issued an edict praising him, and granted him discretionary authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and issued an edict of praise, authorizing Shao to act on his own judgment as local conditions dictated.

sentences.zh: 紹與王世充、蕭銑疆界連接，紹之士卒為賊所虜者，輒見殺害。

translations.literal: Shao's borders adjoined those of Wang Shichong and Xiao Xian. Shao's soldiers captured by the rebels were invariably killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's territory bordered the domains of Wang Shichong and Xiao Xian, and whenever his soldiers fell into rebel hands they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 紹執敵人，皆資給而遣之，賊感其義，不復侵掠，闔境獲安。

translations.literal: When Shao captured enemy soldiers, he supplied them with provisions and sent them back. The rebels were moved by his righteousness and no longer raided; the whole territory was secured in peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao took enemy prisoners, he provided for them and sent them home. The rebels, moved by his magnanimity, ceased their raids, and the entire region knew peace.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭之擊蕭銑也，復令紹督兵以圖荊州，會卒於軍，高祖聞而流涕。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong attacked Xiao Xian, [Gaozu] again ordered Shao to command troops to target Jing Prefecture. He happened to die in the army; when Gaozu heard of it, he wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiaogong of Zhao attacked Xiao Xian, Gaozu again ordered Shao to command troops against Jing Prefecture. Shao died in camp; when Gaozu heard the news, he wept.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，贈荊州都督。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was posthumously appointed Area Commander of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he was posthumously made area commander of Jing Prefecture.
