sentences.zh: 嫡孫力士襲爵，官至洛州長史，卒。

translations.literal: His legitimate grandson Lishi inherited the title; he reached the office of Long Prefect of Luo Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: His legitimate grandson Lishi inherited the title, rose to long prefect of Luo Prefecture, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子欽寂嗣，萬歲登封年為夔州都督府長史。

translations.literal: His son Qinji succeeded; in the Wansui Dengfeng era he served as Long Prefect of the Area Command headquarters at Kui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's son Qinji succeeded to the title; in the Wansui Dengfeng reign he served as long prefect of the Kui Prefecture area command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時契丹入寇，以欽寂兼龍山軍討擊副使，軍次崇州，戰敗被擒。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan invaded; Qinji was appointed deputy commissioner for punitive action of Longshan Army. The army halted at Chong Prefecture, was defeated in battle, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border, Qinji was named deputy commissioner of the Longshan punitive force. His army encamped at Chong Prefecture, was defeated, and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其後，賊將圍安東，令欽寂說屬城之未下者。

translations.literal: Afterwards, as rebel generals besieged Andong, they ordered Qinji to persuade the dependent cities that had not yet surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with rebel forces besieging Andong, they sent Qinji to persuade the surrounding towns that still held out.

sentences.zh: 安東都督裴玄珪時在城下，欽寂謂之曰：「狂賊天殃，滅在朝夕，公但謹守勵兵，以全忠節。」

translations.literal: Andong Area Commander Pei Xuangui was then below the walls. Qinji said to him: "These mad rebels are heaven's scourge; their destruction is within days. My lord need only guard diligently and rouse the troops to preserve loyalty and integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Andong Area Commander Pei Xuangui was then outside the walls. Qinji told him: "These mad rebels are heaven's curse—their ruin is near. Hold firm, drill your men, and keep your loyalty intact."

sentences.zh: 賊大怒，遂害之。

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly enraged and thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were enraged and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 則天下制褒美，贈蘄州刺史，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Empress Wu then issued an edict of praise; he was posthumously appointed Prefect of Qi Prefecture, with posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu issued an edict commending him, posthumously made him prefect of Qi Prefecture, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 又授其子輔乾左監門衛中候，仍為海東慰勞使；

translations.literal: [She] also appointed his son Fuqian Middle Guard of the Left Gate Guard Directorate, and additionally made him envoy to comfort the eastern sea region;
translations.idiomatic: She also appointed his son Fuqian middle guard in the Left Gate Guard Directorate and made him commissioner to console the eastern frontier;

sentences.zh: 令迎其喪柩，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: [She] ordered that his coffin be escorted back and reburied according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered his coffin brought home and reburied with full honors.

sentences.zh: 輔乾，開元中官至光祿卿。

translations.literal: Fuqian, during the Kaiyuan era reached the office of Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Fuqian rose to minister of imperial entertainments during the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 紹次子智仁，初，以父勳授溫州刺史，封孝昌縣公。

translations.literal: Shao's second son Zhiren—at first, through his father's merit he was appointed Prefect of Wen Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiaochang County.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's second son Zhiren was first made prefect of Wen Prefecture and created Duke of Xiaochang County in recognition of his father's service.

sentences.zh: 尋繼其父為硤州刺史，後歷太僕少卿、涼州都督。

translations.literal: Soon after he succeeded his father as Prefect of Xia Prefecture; later he served successively as Vice Minister of the Stud and Area Commander of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon succeeded his father as prefect of Xia Prefecture and later served as vice minister of the stud and area commander of Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 紹少子圉師，有器干，博涉藝文，舉進士。

translations.literal: Shao's youngest son Yusshi had capacity and ability, broadly versed in arts and letters, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's youngest son Yusshi was talented and capable, widely read in literature and the arts, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，累遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was promoted through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrently Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 657 he rose through the ranks to vice minister of the palace secretariat, third-rank chancellor, and concurrent compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 三年，以修實錄功封平恩縣男，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: In the third year, for merit in compiling the Veritable Records he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ping'en County and granted three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, for his work on the veritable records, he was created baron of Ping'en County and given three hundred bolts of silk and goods.

sentences.zh: 四遷，龍朔中為左相。

translations.literal: After four further promotions, in the Longshuo era he became Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After four more promotions he became left chancellor during the Longshuo reign.

sentences.zh: 俄以子自然因獵射殺人，隱而不奏，又為李義府所擠，左遷虔州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, because his son Ziran killed a man while hunting and Yusshi concealed it without reporting, and also because he was squeezed out by Li Yifu, he was demoted to Prefect of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his son Ziran killed someone during a hunting outing, and Yusshi concealed the crime instead of reporting it. Pressured by Li Yifu, he was demoted to prefect of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 政存寬惠，人吏刊石以頌之。

translations.literal: His administration emphasized leniency and kindness; officials and commoners carved stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and kindness, and officials and commoners erected stone monuments in his praise.

sentences.zh: 嘗有官吏犯贓事露，圉師不令推究，但賜清白詩以激之，犯者愧懼，遂改節為廉士，其寬厚如此。

translations.literal: Once when an official's corruption was exposed, Yusshi would not have it investigated but only bestowed a poem on integrity to stir him; the offender felt shame and fear and thereupon changed his ways to become an upright man—such was his leniency and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: When an official's bribery came to light, Yusshi would not launch an investigation but instead gave him a poem on integrity. Shamed and fearful, the man reformed and became an upright official—such was Yusshi's forbearance.

sentences.zh: 上元中，再遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was again promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan reign he was promoted again to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年卒，贈幽州都督，陪葬恭陵，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yifeng he died; posthumously appointed Area Commander of You Prefecture, buried with honor at Gongling, posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 679, was posthumously made area commander of You Prefecture, buried at Empress Gaozong's Gongling Mausoleum, and given the posthumous title Simple.

sentences.zh: 李襲志，字重光，本隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Li Xizhi, courtesy name Chongguang, was originally a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xizhi, courtesy name Chongguang, was originally from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 五葉祖景避地安康，復稱金州安康人也。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Jing took refuge in Ankang; thereafter [the family] called themselves natives of Ankang in Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations back his ancestor Jing had fled to Ankang, and the family thereafter regarded itself as from Ankang in Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周信州總管、安康郡公遷哲孫也。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Qianzhe, Zhou Grand Commander of Xin Prefecture and Duke of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Qianzhe, who had served as grand commander of Xin Prefecture under Northern Zhou and held the title Duke of Ankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父敬猷，隋台州刺史、安康郡公。

translations.literal: His father Jingyou was Prefect of Tai Prefecture under Sui and Duke of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingyou had been prefect of Tai Prefecture under the Sui and held the title Duke of Ankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 襲志，初任隋歷始安郡丞。

translations.literal: Xizhi's first office under Sui was as Assistant Prefect of Shi'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi's first Sui appointment was as assistant prefect of Shi'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大業末，江外盜賊尤甚，襲志散家產，招募得三千人，以守郡城。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, bandits beyond the river were especially severe. Xizhi dispersed his family property, recruited three thousand men, and used them to defend the commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye, banditry was rampant south of the Yangzi. Xizhi spent his family fortune to raise three thousand men and hold the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 時蕭銑、林士弘、曹武徹等爭來攻擊，襲志固守久之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Xian, Lin Shihong, Cao Wuche, and others competed in coming to attack; Xizhi held firm for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian, Lin Shihong, Cao Wuche, and others repeatedly assaulted him, but Xizhi held out for a long time.

sentences.zh: 後聞宇文化及弒逆，乃集士庶舉哀三日。

translations.literal: Later, hearing of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he gathered officials and commoners to mourn for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he gathered officials and commoners for three days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 有郡人勸襲志曰；

translations.literal: A man of the commandery urged Xizhi, saying:
translations.idiomatic: One local man urged Xizhi, saying:

sentences.zh: 「公累葉冠族，久臨鄙郡，蠻夷畏威，士女悅服，雖曰隋臣，實我之君長。

translations.literal: "My lord, for generations a leading clan, long governing this humble commandery—the barbarians fear your authority, gentlemen and commoners are pleased and obedient. Though called a Sui minister, in truth you are our lord and chief.
translations.idiomatic: "Your house has been a leading clan for generations, and you have long governed this remote commandery. The frontier peoples respect your authority and the people trust you. Though you are formally a Sui official, you are in truth our true ruler.

sentences.zh: 今江都篡逆，四海鼎沸，王號者非止一人，公宜因此時據有嶺表，則百越之人皆拱手向化。

translations.literal: Now Jiangdu has witnessed usurpation; the four seas boil like a cauldron. Those who have taken royal titles are more than one. My lord ought to seize Lingnan at this time—then the peoples of Baiyue will all bow and turn to your rule.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdu has fallen to treason, the empire is in turmoil, and more than one man has claimed a throne. Seize Lingnan now, and the peoples of the south will willingly submit.

sentences.zh: 追蹤尉佗，亦千載一遇也。」

translations.literal: To follow in the footsteps of Zhao Tuo is also a meeting of a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: To emulate Zhao Tuo would be the opportunity of a lifetime."

sentences.zh: 襲志厲聲曰：「吾世樹忠貞，見危授命，今雖江都陷沒，而宗社猶存，當與諸君戮力中原，共雪仇恥，豈可怙亂稱兵，以圖不義！

translations.literal: Xizhi said in a stern voice: "Our house for generations has planted loyalty and integrity; in facing danger we give our lives. Though Jiangdu has fallen, the altars of state still stand. I ought to exert all strength with you gentlemen in the Central Plains to wipe away shame and avenge outrage—how can I rely on disorder and raise arms to pursue what is unrighteous!
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi said sharply: "My family has upheld loyalty for generations—we meet danger by giving our lives. Jiangdu may be lost, but the dynasty still stands. We should join forces in the Central Plains to avenge this outrage—how could I seize on chaos and take up arms for an unworthy cause!

sentences.zh: 吾寧蹈忠而死，不為逆節而求生。

translations.literal: I would rather tread the path of loyalty and die than preserve my life through treasonous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die in loyalty than live by treason.

sentences.zh: 尉佗愚鄙無識，何足景慕？」

translations.literal: Zhao Tuo was stupid, base, and without understanding—what is there worth admiring?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tuo was a crude and shortsighted man—why should I look up to him?"

sentences.zh: 於是欲斬勸者，從眾議而止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wished to behead the one who urged him, but stopped at the crowd's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to execute the man who had urged him, but yielded to others' counsel and stopped.

sentences.zh: 襲志固守，經二年而無援，卒為蕭銑所陷，銑署為工部尚書、檢校桂州總管。

translations.literal: Xizhi held firm; after two years without reinforcements he was finally overrun by Xiao Xian. Xiao appointed him Minister of Public Works and Acting Area Commander of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi held out for two years without aid and was finally taken by Xiao Xian, who appointed him minister of public works and acting area commander of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武德初，高祖遣其子玄嗣齎書召之，襲志乃密說嶺南首領隨永平郡守李光度與之歸國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Gaozu sent his son Xuansi bearing a letter to summon him. Xizhi then secretly persuaded the Lingnan chieftains, following Yongping Commandery Prefect Li Guangdu, to return to the [Tang] state with him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign Gaozu sent his son Xuansi with a letter summoning Xizhi. Xizhi then secretly persuaded the Lingnan chiefs, led by Yongping prefect Li Guangdu, to submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 高祖又令間使齎書諭襲志曰：「卿昔久在桂州，仍屬隋室運終，四方圮絕，率眾保境，未知所統。

translations.literal: Gaozu also sent a secret envoy bearing a letter instructing Xizhi: "You long served in Gui Prefecture. It was still the time when the Sui house's fortune ended; the four directions were cut off. You led the masses to guard the borders, not knowing whom you served.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu also sent a secret envoy with a letter to Xizhi: "You long held Gui Prefecture when the Sui dynasty was failing and the empire was cut off in all directions. You led your people in holding the frontier, uncertain whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 朕撫臨天下，志在綏育，眷彼幽遐，思沾聲教。

translations.literal: I now oversee all under Heaven, my intent to soothe and nurture. I cherish those distant and remote regions and wish to extend to them the sound of my teachings.
translations.idiomatic: I now rule the realm with the aim of bringing peace and nurture to all. I care for those far-off lands and wish to extend my rule and culture to them.

sentences.zh: 況卿朕之宗姓，情異於常。

translations.literal: Moreover, you share my surname of the imperial clan—our bond is not ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you bear my own clan name—our bond is not an ordinary one.

sentences.zh: 家弟侄並立誠效公，又分遣首領，申諭諸州，情深奉國，甚副所望。

translations.literal: My younger brothers and nephews have all pledged sincerity and served loyally; they have also dispatched leaders separately to announce and instruct the various prefectures. Your deep devotion in serving the state greatly fulfills my hopes.
translations.idiomatic: My brothers and nephews have already sworn loyalty to the cause, and they have sent leaders throughout the region to rally the prefectures. Your devotion to the state fully matches what I hoped for.

sentences.zh: 卿之子弟，並據州縣，俱展誠績，每所嘉嘆，不能已已。

translations.literal: Your sons and younger brothers all hold prefectures and counties, each showing loyal achievement. Each time I hear of it I sigh with praise and cannot cease.
translations.idiomatic: Your sons and brothers hold prefectures and counties throughout the region, and each has shown loyal service. I am delighted each time I hear of it and cannot express my praise enough.

sentences.zh: 令併入屬籍，著於宗正。」

translations.literal: [I] order that you all be entered together into the clan register and recorded with the Directorate of the Imperial Clan."
translations.idiomatic: I order that you all be enrolled in the imperial clan register under the Directorate of the Imperial Clan."

sentences.zh: 及蕭銑平，江南道大使、趙郡王孝恭授襲志桂州總管。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian was pacified, the Jiangnan Circuit Commissioner, Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong, appointed Xizhi Area Commander of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Xian was defeated, Prince Xiaogong of Zhao, commissioner of the Jiangnan circuit, appointed Xizhi area commander of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武德五年入朝，授柱國，封始安郡公，拜江州都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude he entered court; he was granted the title Bulwark of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Shi'an Commandery, and appointed Area Commander of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 622 he went to court, was granted the bulwark title, created Duke of Shi'an Commandery, and appointed area commander of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及輔公祏反，又以襲志為水軍總管討平之，轉桂州都督。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, [Gaozu] again appointed Xizhi Grand Commander of the Navy to suppress and pacify him; he was then transferred to Area Commander of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, Xizhi was again named grand commander of the navy to suppress him; afterward he returned as area commander of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 襲志前後凡任桂州二十八載，政尚清簡，嶺外安之。

translations.literal: Xizhi in all served at Gui Prefecture for twenty-eight years; his administration favored clarity and simplicity, and the region beyond the mountains was settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi served at Gui Prefecture for twenty-eight years in all. His rule was plain and restrained, and the Lingnan frontier was kept at peace.

sentences.zh: 後表請入朝，拜右光祿大夫、行汾州刺史致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he memorialized requesting to enter court; he was appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Acting Prefect of Fen Prefecture, then retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later petitioned to retire to court, was made right grand master for splendid happiness and acting prefect of Fen Prefecture, retired from office, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 襲志弟襲譽。

translations.literal: Xizhi's younger brother was Xiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi's younger brother was Xiyu.

sentences.zh: 襲譽，字茂實，少通敏，有識度。

translations.literal: Xiyu, courtesy name Maoshi, was in youth quick and perceptive, with discernment and breadth of judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyu, courtesy name Maoshi, was quick and perceptive as a youth and showed sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 隋末為冠軍府司兵。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he served as Army Aide of the Champion Guard headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he served as army aide of the Champion Guard headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時陰世師輔代王為京師留守，所在盜賊蜂起，襲譽說世師遣兵據永豐倉，發粟以賑窮乏，出庫物賞戰士，移檄郡縣，同心討賊。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Shishi assisted the Prince of Dai in holding the capital as defender. Bandits rose like bees everywhere. Xiyu urged Shishi to dispatch troops to seize the Yongfeng Granary, release grain to relieve the destitute, distribute storehouse goods to reward warriors, and send proclamations to commanderies and counties to unite in heart in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shishi was then defending the capital on behalf of the Prince of Dai while bandits rose everywhere. Xiyu urged him to seize the Yongfeng Granary, open the stores to feed the needy, reward soldiers from the treasury, and issue calls to the surrounding commanderies to join in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 世師不能用，乃求外出募山南士馬，世師許之。

translations.literal: Shishi could not adopt [the plan]; [Xiyu] then requested to go out and recruit soldiers and horses from south of the mountains, and Shishi granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi would not act on the advice, so Xiyu asked leave to go out and raise troops and horses from south of the Qinling; Shishi agreed.

sentences.zh: 既至漢中，會高祖定長安，召授太府少卿，封安康郡公，仍令與兄襲志附籍於宗正。

translations.literal: When he reached Hanzhong, it happened that Gaozu had secured Chang'an. [Gaozu] summoned him and appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, enfeoffed him as Duke of Ankang Commandery, and additionally ordered him and his elder brother Xizhi to attach their registration to the Imperial Clan Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Hanzhong just as Gaozu secured Chang'an, he was summoned, made vice minister of the imperial storehouse, and created Duke of Ankang Commandery; he and his brother Xizhi were also enrolled in the imperial clan register.

sentences.zh: 太宗討王世充，以襲譽為潞州總管。

translations.literal: When Taizong attacked Wang Shichong, he appointed Xiyu Area Commander of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Wang Shichong, he made Xiyu area commander of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時突厥與國和親，又通使於世充，襲譽掩擊，悉斬之。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks were in marital alliance with the [Tang] state but also sent envoys to Shichong. Xiyu launched a surprise attack and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were then allied with Tang by marriage but also sent envoys to Wang Shichong. Xiyu intercepted them in an ambush and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 因委令轉運以饋大軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon [Taizong] entrusted him with transport to supply the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then put him in charge of supply lines to feed the main army.

sentences.zh: 後歷光祿卿、浦州刺史，轉揚州大都督府長史，為江南道巡察大使，多所黜陟。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Minister of Imperial Entertainments and Prefect of Pu Prefecture, then became Long Prefect of the Great Area Command headquarters at Yang Prefecture; as Inspector of the Jiangnan Circuit he promoted and demoted many officials.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as minister of imperial entertainments and prefect of Pu Prefecture, then as long prefect of the Yangzhou area command headquarters and inspector of the Jiangnan circuit, promoting and demoting many officials.

sentences.zh: 江都俗好商賈，不事農桑。

translations.literal: The custom of Jiangdu favored merchants and did not attend to farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jiangdu favored trade over agriculture.

sentences.zh: 襲譽乃引雷陂水，又築勾城塘，溉田八百餘頃，百姓獲其利。

translations.literal: Xiyu then diverted the waters of Lei Marsh, also built the Gougeng Pond, irrigated more than eight hundred qing of fields, and the common people received its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyu channeled water from Lei Marsh and built the Gougeng reservoir, irrigating more than eight hundred qing of farmland and bringing real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 召拜太府卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed minister of the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 襲譽性嚴整，所在以威肅聞。

translations.literal: Xiyu was stern and disciplined by nature; wherever he served he was known for imposing authority.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyu was stern and disciplined, and wherever he served he was known for strict authority.

sentences.zh: 凡獲俸祿，必散之宗親，其餘資多寫書而已。

translations.literal: Whenever he received salary and emoluments, he always distributed them among clan relatives; of the remainder he mostly spent on copying books.
translations.idiomatic: He always distributed his salary among his kinsmen; whatever remained he spent chiefly on copying books.

sentences.zh: 及從揚州罷職，經史遂盈數車。

translations.literal: When he left his post at Yang Prefecture, the classics and histories filled several cartloads.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he left his Yangzhou post, his copies of the classics and histories filled several cartloads.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂子孫曰：「吾近京城有賜田十頃，耕之可以充食；

translations.literal: Once he told his descendants: "I have near the capital ten qing of granted fields; by farming them one can fill one's belly;
translations.idiomatic: He once told his descendants: "Near the capital I have ten qing of granted land—farm it and you will have enough to eat;

sentences.zh: 河內有賜桑千樹，蠶之可以充衣；

translations.literal: in Henei there are a thousand granted mulberry trees; by raising silkworms one can fill one's clothing;
translations.idiomatic: in Henei I have a thousand granted mulberry trees—raise silkworms and you will have enough to wear;

sentences.zh: 江東所寫之書，讀之可以求官。

translations.literal: the books copied in Jiangdong—by reading them one can seek office.
translations.idiomatic: and the books I copied in Jiangdong—study them and you can win office.

sentences.zh: 吾沒之後，爾曹但能勤此三事，亦何羨於人！」

translations.literal: After my death, if you can only be diligent in these three things, what need is there to envy others!"
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, if you keep at these three things, what need have you to envy anyone else!"

sentences.zh: 尋轉涼州都督，加金紫光祿大夫，行同州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Area Commander of Liang Prefecture, given the additional rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag and Purple Border, and Acting Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to area commander of Liang Prefecture, given the additional rank of grand master for splendid happiness with the golden bag and purple border, and made acting prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐在涼州陰憾番禾縣丞劉武，杖而殺之，至是有司議當死，制除名，流於泉州，無幾而卒。

translations.literal: He was convicted because at Liang Prefecture he bore a secret grudge against Fanhe County Assistant Liu Wu and beat him to death. When the matter came to trial, the relevant offices judged he deserved death; an edict stripped his name [from the registers] and exiled him to Quan Prefecture; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: While area commander of Liang Prefecture he had nursed a private grudge against Fanhe county assistant Liu Wu and beat him to death. The courts ruled he deserved death; he was stripped of rank and exiled to Quan Prefecture, where he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 撰《五經妙言》四十捲、《江東記》三十捲、《忠孝圖》二十捲。

translations.literal: He compiled "Subtle Sayings on the Five Classics" in forty juan, "Records of Jiangdong" in thirty juan, and "Illustrations of Loyalty and Filial Piety" in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Subtle Sayings on the Five Classics in forty juan, Records of Jiangdong in thirty juan, and Illustrations of Loyalty and Filial Piety in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 兄子懷儼，頗以文才著名。

translations.literal: His brother's son Huaiyan was quite renowned for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Huaiyan was widely known for his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 歷蘭台侍郎，受制檢校寫四部書進內，以書有汙，左授郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Orchid Terrace; by imperial order he was assigned to supervise the copying of the books of the Four Libraries to be submitted to the palace. Because the books were soiled, he was demoted and appointed Prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the Orchid Terrace and, by imperial order, supervised the copying of the Four Libraries' books for submission to the palace. When the copies were found soiled, he was demoted to prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後卒於禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 姜抃，秦州上邽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Bian was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bian was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖真，後魏南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Governor of Southern Qin Prefecture under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had been governor of Southern Qin Prefecture under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父景，周梁州總管、建平郡公。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Grand Governor of Liang Prefecture under Zhou and Duke of Jianping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had been grand governor of Liang Prefecture under Northern Zhou and Duke of Jianping commandery.

sentences.zh: 抃，大業末為晉陽長，會高祖留守太原，見抃深器之。

translations.literal: Bian, in the final years of the Daye reign era, served as Magistrate of Jinyang. When Emperor Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he saw Bian and thought very highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of the Daye era, Bian served as magistrate of Jinyang. When Emperor Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he took a strong liking to Bian.

sentences.zh: 抃退謂所親曰：「隋祚將亡，必有命世大才，以應圖籙，唐公有霸王之度，以吾觀之，必為撥亂之主。」

translations.literal: Bian withdrew and said to those close to him: "The Sui dynasty's mandate is about to perish. There must be a world-conquering great talent to answer the prophecy of the charts and registers. The Duke of Tang has the stature of a hegemon and king. As I see it, he will surely be the lord who sets the realm to order."
translations.idiomatic: Bian withdrew and told his intimates: "The Sui mandate is failing. A world-shaping genius must arise to fulfill the prophecies in the charts and registers. The Duke of Tang has the bearing of a hegemon-king. In my judgment, he is destined to be the one who restores order from chaos."

sentences.zh: 由是深自結納。

translations.literal: From this he drew close and formed a bond.
translations.idiomatic: From that time he cultivated the closest ties with him.

sentences.zh: 及大將軍府建，引為司功參軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Office was established, Bian was recruited as Records Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's Office was established, he was appointed records officer.

sentences.zh: 從平霍邑，拔絳郡，監督大軍濟河。

translations.literal: He followed the campaigns to pacify Huoyi, capture Jiang Commandery, and oversee the main army's crossing of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Huoyi, capturing Jiang commandery, and supervising the main army's river crossing.

sentences.zh: 時兵士爭渡，抃部勒諸軍，自昏至曉，六軍畢濟。

translations.literal: At the time the soldiers struggled to cross; Bian marshaled the armies, and from dusk till dawn all six armies completed the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: As troops scrambled to cross, Bian kept the armies in order; from nightfall until dawn all six armies had crossed.

sentences.zh: 高祖稱嘆之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 平京城，除相國兵曹參軍，封長道縣公。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was appointed Military Staff Officer to the Chancellor of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Changdao County.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was taken, he was made military staff officer to the chancellor of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Changdao county.

sentences.zh: 時薛舉寇秦、隴，以抃西州之望，詔於隴右安撫，承製以便宜從事。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Ju was invading Qin and Long; because of Bian's standing in the western regions, an edict was issued for him to pacify Longyou, with imperial authorization to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju raided Qin and Long, Bian's prestige in the western provinces led to an edict appointing him to pacify Longyou, with discretionary authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 抃將行，奏曰：「天人之望，誠有所歸，願早膺圖籙，以寧兆庶。

translations.literal: As Bian was about to depart, he memorialized: "The hopes of Heaven and the people indeed have their object. I pray Your Majesty will soon receive the mandate of the charts and registers to bring peace to the myriad masses.
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out, Bian memorialized: "Heaven and the people already look to a single destination. I pray Your Majesty will soon receive the mandate foretold in the charts and registers and bring peace to the masses.

sentences.zh: 老夫犬馬暮齒，恐先朝露，得一睹升紫殿，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: This old man, in the twilight of his dog-and-horse years, fears I may meet the morning dew first. If I could but once behold Your Majesty ascend the purple palace, I would die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: I am an old man in the evening of my years and may not live to see the dawn. Grant me but one sight of Your Majesty ascending the purple palace, and I shall die content."

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 抃與竇軌出散關，下河池、漢陽二郡。

translations.literal: Bian and Dou Gui went out through Sanguan Pass and subdued Hechi and Hanyang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Dou Gui marched out through Sanguan Pass and reduced Hechi and Hanyang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 軍次長道，與薛舉相遇，軌輕敵，為舉所敗。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Changdao, they encountered Xue Ju. Dou Gui underestimated the enemy and was defeated by Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Changdao and met Xue Ju. Dou Gui underestimated the enemy and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 征抃還京，拜員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Bian was recalled to the capital and appointed Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was recalled to the capital and appointed supernumerary regular cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 及平薛仁杲，拜抃秦州刺史，高祖謂曰：「衣錦還鄉，古人所尚；

translations.literal: When Xue Rengao was pacified, Bian was appointed Prefect of Qin Prefecture. Emperor Gaozu said to him: "Returning home in brocade robes is what the ancients honored;
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Rengao was subdued, Bian was appointed prefect of Qin Prefecture. Emperor Gaozu told him: "To return home in brocade is what the ancients most admired;

sentences.zh: 今以本州相授，用答元功。

translations.literal: now I grant you your native prefecture to repay your founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: now I give you your home prefecture in reward for your founding service.

sentences.zh: 涼州之路，近為荒梗，宜弘方略，有以靜之。」

translations.literal: The road to Liang Prefecture has lately become desolate and blocked. You should deploy broad strategy to bring quiet there."
translations.idiomatic: The route to Liang Prefecture has lately fallen into ruin and disorder. Apply broad strategy and find a way to restore calm."

sentences.zh: 抃至州，撫以恩信，州人相謂曰：「吾輩復見太平官府矣。」

translations.literal: When Bian reached the prefecture, he governed with kindness and trust. The people of the prefecture said to one another: "We shall again see officials of the age of peace."
translations.idiomatic: When Bian arrived, he ruled with kindness and good faith. The people said among themselves: "We are seeing peaceful government again."

sentences.zh: 盜賊悉來歸首，士庶安之。

translations.literal: All bandits came forward to surrender, and gentry and commoners lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits surrendered in full, and officials and commoners alike were at ease.

sentences.zh: 尋轉隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，以老疾去職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he left office due to age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年卒，贈岷州都督，謚曰安。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Zhenguan. Posthumously he was given the office of Area Commander of Min Prefecture, with the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhenguan. He was posthumously made area commander of Min Prefecture and given the posthumous title An.

sentences.zh: 子行本，貞觀中為將作大匠。

translations.literal: His son Xingben, during the Zhenguan reign, served as Chief Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingben served as chief director of palace construction during the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 太宗修九成、洛陽二宮，行本總領之，以勤濟稱旨，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong renovated the Jiucheng and Luoyang palaces, Xingben oversaw the work. Because his diligence met with approval, he received generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong rebuilt the Jiucheng and Luoyang palaces, Xingben directed the work. His tireless efficiency pleased the emperor, and the rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 有所游幸，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Xingben was always in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On every imperial tour, Xingben was always in attendance.

sentences.zh: 又轉左屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was also transferred to General of the Left Tunwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made general of the Left Tunwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 時太宗選趫捷之士，衣五色袍，乘六閒馬，直屯營以充仗內宿衛，名為「飛騎」，每游幸，即騎以從，分隸於行本。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Taizong selected agile warriors clothed in five-colored robes, riding six fine horses, stationed directly in the encampments as inner palace guards—these were called "Flying Cavalry." Whenever the emperor toured, they rode in attendance, placed under Xingben's command.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then chose swift, agile men, clothed them in five-colored robes, and mounted them on six fine horses. They were posted in the encampments as inner palace guards and called the Flying Cavalry. On every tour they rode in attendance, all placed under Xingben's command.

sentences.zh: 及高昌之役，以行本為行軍副總管，率眾先出伊州。

translations.literal: During the Gaochang campaign, Xingben was made Deputy Campaign Commander and led troops out from Yizhou first.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Gaochang, Xingben was made deputy campaign commander and led the vanguard out from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 未至柳谷百餘里，依山造攻具。

translations.literal: Before reaching Liugu by more than a hundred li, he built siege engines along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred li before Liugu, he built siege engines along the mountain slopes.

sentences.zh: 其處有班超紀功碑，行本磨去其文，更刻頌，陳國威德而去。

translations.literal: At that place was Ban Chao's stele commemorating his achievements. Xingben effaced its text and carved in its place an ode praising the state's prestige and virtue, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: There stood Ban Chao's stele of merit. Xingben ground away the original inscription and carved in its place an ode to the dynasty's majesty and virtue, then moved on.

sentences.zh: 遂與侯君集進平高昌，璽書勞之曰：「攻戰之重，器械為先，將士屬心，待以制敵。

translations.literal: He then joined Hou Junji in pacifying Gaochang. An imperial letter praised him: "In the weight of attack and combat, weapons and equipment come first; the hearts of officers and soldiers depend on them to overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Hou Junji in pacifying Gaochang. An imperial letter of commendation read: "In war, weapons and equipment are paramount; officers and soldiers stake their hearts on them to defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 卿星言就路，躬事修營，干戈才動，梯衝暫臨。

translations.literal: You, upon receiving the order to set out, personally undertook construction and encampment. When the weapons of war had barely moved, ladders and battering rams were already at hand.
translations.idiomatic: You set out at once upon receiving your orders and personally saw to the camps and engines. Hardly had the army stirred before ladders and battering rams stood ready.

sentences.zh: 三軍勇士，因斯樹績；

translations.literal: The brave warriors of the three armies thereby achieved merit;
translations.idiomatic: The three armies' bravest men won their glory thereby;

sentences.zh: 萬里逋寇，用是克平。

translations.literal: the fugitive rebels ten thousand li away were thereby subjugated.
translations.idiomatic: and rebels ten thousand li distant were brought to submission.

sentences.zh: 方之前古，豈足相況！」

translations.literal: Compared with the ancients of old, how could one even mention them!"
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the ancients, what comparison is even possible!"

sentences.zh: 及還，進封金城郡公，賜物一百五十段、奴婢七十人。

translations.literal: When he returned, he was promoted to Duke of Jincheng Commandery and granted one hundred fifty bolts of goods and seventy slaves.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Duke of Jincheng commandery and given one hundred fifty bolts of goods and seventy slaves.

sentences.zh: 十七年，太宗將征高麗，行本諫以為師未可動，太宗不從。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Emperor Taizong was about to campaign against Goguryeo, Xingben remonstrated that the army should not yet move. The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, as Emperor Taizong prepared to campaign against Goguryeo, Xingben argued that the army should not yet march. The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 行本從至蓋牟城，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: Xingben followed him as far as Gaimou Fortress, was struck by a flying arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben accompanied him as far as Gaimou Fortress, where he was struck by a flying arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 太宗賦詩以悼之，贈左衛大將軍、郕國公，謚曰襄，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong composed a poem to mourn him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard, Duke of the State of Bi, with posthumous title Xiang and burial at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong wrote a poem in mourning, posthumously appointing him grand general of the Left Guard and Duke of the State of Bi, with the posthumous title Xiang and burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子簡嗣，永徽中，官至安北都護，卒。

translations.literal: His son Jian succeeded; during Yonghui he rose to Protectorate General of the Pacified North and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him and, in the Yonghui era, rose to Protectorate General of the Pacified North before his death.

sentences.zh: 子晞嗣，開元初左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jian's son Xi succeeded; early in Kaiyuan he was Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Xi succeeded in turn and, early in the Kaiyuan era, served as left regular cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 簡弟柔遠，美姿容，善於敷奏。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Ruyuan had handsome features and was skilled at memorializing the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Ruyuan was handsome in appearance and skilled at presenting memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 則天時，至左鷹揚衛將軍、通事舍人、內供奉。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time he reached General of the Left Yingyang Guard, Palace Herald, and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he rose to general of the Left Yingyang Guard, palace herald, and inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 朕聞士之生代，始於事親，中於事君，終於立身，此其本也。

translations.literal: I have heard that a scholar born into his age begins by serving his parents, continues by serving his lord, and ends by establishing his person—this is the root.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a man born into his age begins by serving his parents, goes on to serve his ruler, and ends by establishing his own character—that is the foundation of life.

sentences.zh: 若乃移孝成忠，策名委質。

translations.literal: One may then transform filial piety into loyalty and register his name to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: From there he may turn filial devotion into loyalty and enroll his name to pledge his service.

sentences.zh: 命有太山之重，義徇則為輕；

translations.literal: When a command bears the weight of Mount Tai, righteousness held to makes it light;
translations.idiomatic: When a command weighs as heavy as Mount Tai, loyalty held firm makes it light;

sentences.zh: 草有疾風之力，節全則知勁。

translations.literal: when grass meets a fierce wind, only when its fiber remains intact does one know its strength.
translations.idiomatic: when grass meets a raging wind, only if its stalk stays whole does one know its strength.

sentences.zh: 況君臣之相遇，而故舊之不遺乎！

translations.literal: How much more when ruler and minister meet, and old ties are not forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when ruler and minister meet and old friendship is not cast aside!

sentences.zh: 銀青光祿大夫、殿中監、楚國公姜皎，簪紱聯華，珪璋特秀。

translations.literal: Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Bag, Director of the Secretariat, Duke of the State of Chu Jiang Jiao—his official posts linked in brilliance, his jade tablet singular in excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Bag, director of the Secretariat, and Duke of the State of Chu, Jiang Jiao—his offices glittered in succession, his talent stood apart like fine jade.

sentences.zh: 寬厚為量，體靜而安仁；

translations.literal: Broadness and generosity were his measure; calm in bearing, he was secure in benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Broadness and generosity were his measure; serene in person, he rested securely in benevolence;

sentences.zh: 精微用心，理和而專直。

translations.literal: refined concentration was his intent; harmonious in principle, he was upright and single-minded.
translations.idiomatic: subtle care was his intent; harmonious in principle, he was upright and resolute.

sentences.zh: 往居籓邸，潛款風雲，亦由彭祖之同書，子陵之共學。

translations.literal: When he had lived in the princely mansion, he secretly aligned himself with the winds and clouds; this was like Pengzu's shared texts and Ziling's shared studies.
translations.idiomatic: While dwelling in the princely mansion he secretly committed himself to great affairs, as Peng Zu once shared texts with his lord and Yan Ziling studied together with his.

sentences.zh: 朕常游幸於外，至長楊、鄠杜之間，皎於此時與之累宿，私謂朕曰：「太上皇即登九五，王必為儲副。」

translations.literal: I often toured abroad, and between Changyang and E and Du, Jiao lodged with me on several nights. He privately told me: "When the Taishang Huang ascends the throne of the Nine-Fives, the Prince will surely become heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: I often traveled abroad, and between Changyang and the districts of E and Du, Jiao stayed with me for many nights. He told me privately: "When the Taishang Huang takes the throne, Your Highness will surely become heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 凡如此者數四，朕叱而後止。

translations.literal: On some four occasions he spoke thus; I rebuked him before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in this way on four occasions before I rebuked him into silence.

sentences.zh: 寧知非僕，雖玩於鄧晨；

translations.literal: Who could know he was not a menial, though he played at Deng Chen's gate;
translations.idiomatic: Who could tell he was no mere servant, though he passed his days in play at Deng Chen's gate;

sentences.zh: 可收護軍，遂訶於硃祐。

translations.literal: one who could accept the Protectorate Army thereupon rebuked Zhu You.
translations.idiomatic: yet one who could take command of the Protectorate Army thereupon rebuked Zhu You.

sentences.zh: 皎復言於朕兄弟及諸駙馬等，因聞徹太上皇，太上皇遽奏於中宗孝和皇帝。

translations.literal: Jiao again spoke to my brothers and the various sons-in-law, and the matter reached the Taishang Huang, who immediately memorialized Zhongzong, the filial and harmonious emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao spoke again to my brothers and the various imperial sons-in-law, and word reached the Taishang Huang, who at once memorialized Emperor Zhongzong, the Filial and Harmonious Emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋遣嗣虢王邕等鞫問，皎保護無怠，辭意轉堅。

translations.literal: Soon the heir to Prince of Guo, Yong, and others were dispatched to investigate and interrogate. Jiao protected him without slackening; his words grew ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the heir to the Prince of Guo, Yong, and others were sent to investigate. Jiao shielded the prince without faltering, and his words grew only firmer.

sentences.zh: 李通之讖記不言，田叔之髡鉗罔憚。

translations.literal: Li Tongzhi did not speak of the omen texts; Tian Shu did not fear the shaved head and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongzhi would not utter the prophecy texts; Tian Shu did not shrink from the shaved head and fetters.

sentences.zh: 仍為宗楚客、紀處訥等密奏，請投皎炎荒。

translations.literal: Still Zong Chuke, Ji Chuna, and others secretly memorialized, asking that Jiao be sent to the fiery wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zong Chuke, Ji Chuna, and others secretly memorialized, asking that Jiao be cast into the burning wilds.

sentences.zh: 中宗特降恩私，左遷潤州長史。

translations.literal: Zhongzong specially showed private favor and demoted him to Chief Administrator of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong showed him special private favor and demoted him to chief administrator of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 讒邪每構，忠懇逾深，戴於朕躬，憂存王室。

translations.literal: Slanderers constantly plotted, yet his loyal earnestness grew ever deeper. He took concern for my person and worried for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers plotted against him again and again, yet his loyal devotion only deepened. He cared for me personally and kept the welfare of the royal house at heart.

sentences.zh: 以為天且有命，預睹成龍之征；

translations.literal: He believed Heaven had a mandate and had foreseen the signs of becoming a dragon;
translations.idiomatic: He believed Heaven had ordained a destiny and had foreseen the signs of the dragon's ascent;

sentences.zh: 人而無禮，常懷逐鳥之志。

translations.literal: yet men without propriety constantly harbored the intent of driving away the bird.
translations.idiomatic: yet men without propriety constantly nursed the wish to drive away the bird.

sentences.zh: 游辭枉陷，旋罹貶斥；

translations.literal: With roving words he was falsely trapped, and soon suffered demotion;
translations.idiomatic: Loose talk falsely ensnared him, and he was soon demoted;

sentences.zh: 嚴憲將及，殆見誅夷。

translations.literal: harsh punishment was about to fall, and he nearly faced execution.
translations.idiomatic: severe punishment was at hand, and he nearly met execution.

sentences.zh: 履危本於初心，遭險期於不貳，雖禍福之際昭然可圖，而艱難之中是所繄賴。

translations.literal: He faced peril from his original intent and, encountering danger, counted on being unwavering. Though the boundary between fortune and disaster was plainly visible, in hardship he was one on whom I relied.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced peril from his first loyalty and, in danger, expected no wavering. Though fortune and disaster lay clearly before him, in hardship he was the man I relied upon.

sentences.zh: 洎朕祗膺寶位，又共翦奸臣，拜以光寵，不忘捴挹，敬愛之極，神明所知。

translations.literal: When I received the precious throne, I again joined in cutting down treacherous ministers, bestowed on him glorious favor, and did not forget his humble origins—the utmost of respect and love, known to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When I received the throne, I again joined in cutting down treacherous ministers, showered him with honors, and did not forget his humble beginnings—the height of reverence and affection, known to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 造膝則曾莫詭隨，匪躬則動多規諫，補朕之闕，斯人孔臧。

translations.literal: When he came near my person he never spoke with artful compliance; sacrificing himself for the ruler, he often remonstrated. In mending my shortcomings, this man is indeed excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In private audience he never spoke with deceitful compliance; giving himself wholly to the ruler, he often remonstrated. In repairing my faults, this man is truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 而悠悠之談，嗷嗷妄作，丑正惡直，竊生於謗，考言詢事，益亮其誠。

translations.literal: Yet idle talk spreads and wild clamor arises; those who hate the upright and detest the straight breed slander. When I examined his words and inquired into the facts, his sincerity shone brighter still.
translations.idiomatic: Yet idle talk spreads and reckless clamor rises; those who hate the upright and loathe the straight breed slander. When I examined his words and looked into the facts, his sincerity shone all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 昔漢昭帝之保霍光，魏太祖之明程昱，朕之不德，庶幾於此。

translations.literal: In olden days Emperor Zhao of Han preserved Huo Guang, and Emperor Wu of Wei was clear-eyed toward Cheng Yu—my lack of virtue barely approaches this.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Zhao of Han preserved Huo Guang, and Cao Cao saw clearly the worth of Cheng Yu—my own virtue scarcely reaches that level.

sentences.zh: 矧夫否當其悔，則滅宗毀族，朕負之必深；

translations.literal: Moreover, if one rejects what one later regrets, then clans are destroyed and families ruined—my debt to him would run very deep;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if I were to reject him and later repent, clans would be destroyed and families ruined—I would owe him a debt beyond measure;

sentences.zh: 泰至其亨，則如山如河，朕酬之未補。

translations.literal: if peace comes to its fullest prosperity, then like mountains and rivers, my repayment of him would still be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: if peace reaches its fullest height, then like mountains and rivers my repayment would still fall short.

sentences.zh: 豈流言之足聽，而厚德之遂忘？

translations.literal: How could floating words be worth heeding, and thick virtue then be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: How could floating rumors be worth hearing, and deep virtue then be forgotten?

sentences.zh: 謀始有之，圖終可也。

translations.literal: The beginning was planned with him in mind; the end may also be secured.
translations.idiomatic: He was with me at the beginning; let him remain to the end.

sentences.zh: 宜告示中外，咸令知悉。

translations.literal: This should be proclaimed within and without, that all may know.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the court and the realm, that all may know.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常卿，監修國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and Supervisor of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to minister of ceremonies and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 弟晦，又歷御史中丞、吏部侍郎，兄弟當朝用事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui also served successively as Imperial Censor and Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; the brothers held power in court.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hui also served in turn as imperial censor and vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel; the brothers wielded power at court.

sentences.zh: 侍中宋璟以其權寵太盛，恐非久安之道，屢奏請稍抑損之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Song Jing, because their privilege and favor were too great, feared this was not a path to lasting peace, and repeatedly memorialized asking that they be somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Song Jing, fearing that their power and favor were too great to endure, repeatedly memorialized asking that they be somewhat restrained.

sentences.zh: 開元五年下敕曰：「西漢諸將，多以權貴不全；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan an edict was issued: "In the Western Han, many generals, because of their power and high rank, did not survive intact;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan an edict was issued: "Under the Western Han, many generals, because of power and high rank, did not die natural deaths;

sentences.zh: 南陽故人，並以優閒自保。

translations.literal: the old friends of Nanyang all preserved themselves through leisure and ease.
translations.idiomatic: the old companions of Nanyang all preserved themselves through leisure and ease.

sentences.zh: 觀夫先後之跡，吉凶之數，較然可知，良有以也。

translations.literal: Observing the traces of former and latter, the numbers of fortune and misfortune—clearly they can be compared, and there is good reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Compare the records of earlier and later times and the tally of fortune and misfortune—clearly the pattern can be seen, and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、上柱國、楚國公、監修國史姜皎，衣纓奕代，忠讜立誠，精識比於橋玄，密私方於硃祐。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of the State of Chu, Supervisor of the National History Jiang Jiao—robes and tassels splendid through generations, loyal and outspoken in establishing sincerity; keen insight comparable to Qiao Xuan, private loyalty like Zhu You.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of ceremonies, supreme pillar of the state, Duke of the State of Chu, and supervisor of the national history, Jiang Jiao—his robes and tassels shone through generations; he established his loyalty in frank speech; his keen insight matched Qiao Xuan, his private devotion recalled Zhu You.

sentences.zh: 朕昔在籓邸，早申款洽，當謂我以不遺，亦起予以自愛。

translations.literal: When I was in the princely mansion I early formed a sincere bond with him. I thought he held me without discard, and he also roused me to self-regard.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the princely mansion I formed an early bond of trust with him. I believed he held me in esteem without casting me aside, and he also stirred me to value myself.

sentences.zh: 及膺大位，屢錫崇班，茅土列爵，山河傳誓，備蒙光寵，時冠等夷。

translations.literal: When I assumed the great throne I repeatedly bestowed exalted ranks; fiefs and peerages, oaths on mountains and rivers—he was fully showered with glorious favor, for a time chief among his peers.
translations.idiomatic: When I took the throne I repeatedly bestowed exalted ranks—fiefs and peerages, oaths sworn on mountains and rivers. He was showered with honors and for a time stood above his peers.

sentences.zh: 朕每欲戒盈，用克終吉。

translations.literal: I have wished to guard against excess, to attain a fortunate end.
translations.idiomatic: I have wished to guard against excess so that good fortune may last to the end.

sentences.zh: 未若避榮公府，守靖私第，自弘高尚之風，不涉囂塵之境，沐我恩貸，庇爾子孫。

translations.literal: Better to leave the glory of the public offices, keep peace in one's private residence, oneself display the wind of lofty integrity, not tread the realm of clamor and dust, bathe in my grace and favor, and shelter your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave the glory of public office, keep to the quiet of your private home, show forth the spirit of lofty integrity, and not enter the noisy world of power—bathe in my grace and shelter your descendants.

sentences.zh: 宜放歸田園，以恣娛樂。」

translations.literal: You should be released to your fields and gardens to indulge in pleasure as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: You should be released to your fields and gardens to enjoy yourself as you please."

sentences.zh: 又遷晦為宗正卿，以去其權。

translations.literal: Hui was also transferred to Director of the Imperial Clan, thereby removing their power.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was also transferred to director of the imperial clan, thereby stripping them of power.

sentences.zh: 久之，皎復起為秘書監。

translations.literal: After a long while Jiao was again raised as Director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Jiao was again appointed director of the Secretariat library.

sentences.zh: 十年，坐漏洩禁中語，為嗣濮王嶠所奏，敕中書門下究其狀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was convicted of divulging forbidden words spoken within the palace. He was memorialized by the heir to Prince of Pu, Qiao, and the Secretariat and Chancellery were ordered to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was convicted of leaking forbidden words from within the palace. The heir to the Prince of Pu, Qiao, memorialized against him, and the Secretariat and Chancellery were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 嶠，即王守一之妹夫；

translations.literal: Qiao was the brother-in-law of Wang Shouyi;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was the brother-in-law of Wang Shouyi;

sentences.zh: 中書令張嘉貞希守一意，構成其罪，仍奏請先決杖配流嶺外。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiazhen, courting Shouyi's favor, fabricated Jiao's crime and still memorialized asking that he first be publicly flogged and then exiled beyond the Ling mountain range.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhang Jiazhen, seeking Wang Shouyi's favor, fabricated Jiao's guilt and memorialized that he first be flogged and then exiled beyond the Ling mountains.

sentences.zh: 下制曰：「秘書監姜皎，往屬艱難，頗效誠信，功則可錄，寵是以加。

translations.literal: An edict was issued, saying: "Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jiao, in former days amid hardship, rendered considerable loyalty and trustworthiness; his achievements may be recorded, and favor was therefore increased upon him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jiao, in former days amid hardship, showed considerable loyalty and trustworthiness. His achievements deserve to be recorded, and favor was therefore heaped upon him.

sentences.zh: 既忘滿盈之誡，又虧靜慎之道，假說休咎，妄談宮掖。

translations.literal: He has forgotten the warning against fullness and excess, and has fallen short of the way of quiet caution, falsely speaking of fortune and misfortune and recklessly discussing the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He has forgotten the warning against fullness and excess and fallen short of quiet caution, falsely speaking of fortune and misfortune and recklessly discussing affairs of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 據其作孽，合處極刑，念茲舊勳，免此殊死。

translations.literal: Judging by the crimes he has committed, he ought to receive the extreme penalty; mindful of his former merit, he is spared this special death.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the crimes he has committed, he ought to receive the death penalty; mindful of his former merit, he is spared execution.

sentences.zh: 宜決一頓，配流欽州。」

translations.literal: He should receive one beating with the rod and be sentenced to exile in Qin Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: He shall receive one beating with the rod and be exiled to Qin Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 皎既決杖，行至汝州而卒，年五十餘。

translations.literal: After Jiao had been beaten with the rod, he died on the road at Ru Prefecture, aged a little over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: After the beating, Jiao died on the road at Ru Prefecture, aged a little over fifty.

sentences.zh: 皎之所親都水使者劉承祖，配流雷州，自余流死者數人。

translations.literal: Jiao's intimate, the Commissioner of Waterways Liu Chengzu, was sentenced to exile in Lei Prefecture; several others among those exiled also died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's intimate, Commissioner of Waterways Liu Chengzu, was exiled to Lei Prefecture; several others among those exiled also died.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷頗以皎為冤，而咎嘉貞焉。

translations.literal: At the time the court largely regarded Jiao as wronged and blamed Jia Zhen for it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court largely regarded Jiao as wronged and blamed Jia Zhen.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜時為侍中，不能有所持正，論者亦深譏之。

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao was then Attendant-in-Chief but could not uphold what was right; commentators also deeply criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao was then attendant-in-chief but could not uphold what was right; commentators also deeply criticized him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗復思皎舊勳，令遞其柩還，以禮葬之，仍遣中使存問其家。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong again recalled Jiao's former merit, ordered his coffin escorted back, buried him with ceremony, and still sent a palace envoy to inquire after his family.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong again recalled Jiao's former merit, ordered his coffin escorted back, buried him with full ceremony, and sent a palace envoy to inquire after his family.

sentences.zh: 十五年，追贈澤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was posthumously given the post of Inspector of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was posthumously made inspector of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晦坐皎左遷春州司馬，俄遷海州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Hui, implicated through Jiao, was demoted to Vice Governor of Chun Prefecture, soon transferred to Inspector of Hai Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, implicated through Jiao, was demoted to vice governor of Chun Prefecture, soon made inspector of Hai Prefecture, and died there.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：或問屈突通盡忠於隋而功立於唐，事兩國而名愈彰者，何也？

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: Someone asked why Qu Tutong was utterly loyal to Sui yet established merit under Tang, serving two states while his fame grew ever brighter—how was this?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Someone asked why Qu Tutong was utterly loyal to Sui yet established his merit under Tang, serving two states while his fame only grew—how was this?

sentences.zh: 答雲，若立純誠，遇明主，一心可事百君，寧限於兩國爾！

translations.literal: The answer was that if one establishes pure sincerity and meets a enlightened sovereign, one heart may serve a hundred lords—why be limited to two states alone!
translations.idiomatic: The answer was that if one establishes pure sincerity and meets an enlightened sovereign, one heart may serve a hundred lords—why be limited to two states alone!

sentences.zh: 被稠桑之擒，臨難無苟免；

translations.literal: Captured at Chousang, he faced hardship without seeking easy escape;
translations.idiomatic: Captured at Chousang, he faced hardship without seeking easy escape;

sentences.zh: 破仁杲之眾，臨財無苟得，君子哉！

translations.literal: when he broke the host of Ren Gao, he faced wealth without grasping what was not his—a gentleman indeed!
translations.idiomatic: when he broke Ren Gao's army, he faced wealth without grasping what was not his—a gentleman indeed!

sentences.zh: 任瑰、丘和、許紹、李襲志咸遇真主，得為故人，或敘舊立功，或率眾歸國。

translations.literal: Ren Gui, Qiu He, Xu Shao, and Li Xizhi all met a true sovereign and became old acquaintances; some recounted past ties and established merit, others led their hosts to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui, Qiu He, Xu Shao, and Li Xizhi all met a true sovereign and became old acquaintances; some drew on past ties to establish merit, others led their followers home to the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 尋其履跡，皆有可稱。

translations.literal: Tracing their footsteps, each has something worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing their careers, each has something worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 襲志為政，襲譽訓子，庶幾弘遠矣。

translations.literal: Xizhi in governance and Xiyu in instructing his sons were, one may hope, far-reaching indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi in governance and Xiyu in instructing his sons were, one may hope, achievements of far-reaching consequence.

sentences.zh: 姜抃恩信，有能官之譽；

translations.literal: Jiang Bian in kindness and trust had the reputation of a capable official;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bian won a reputation as a capable official through kindness and trust;

sentences.zh: 行本勤濟，多克敵之功。

translations.literal: Xingben was diligent in bringing relief and had many achievements in defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben was diligent in bringing relief and won many victories over the enemy.

sentences.zh: 皎雖故舊，恩幸不倫，雖嘉貞致冤，亦冒寵自掇，豈非無德而祿，福過災生之驗歟！

translations.literal: Jiao, though an old acquaintance, received favor out of all proportion; though Jia Zhen brought about his wrongful treatment, he also courted favor and seized it for himself—is this not the proof that emolument without virtue brings disaster when fortune exceeds its measure!
translations.idiomatic: Jiao, though an old acquaintance, received favor out of all proportion; though Jia Zhen brought about his wrongful treatment, he also courted favor and seized it for himself—is this not proof that emolument without virtue invites disaster when fortune exceeds its measure!

sentences.zh: 任瑰縱妒妻無禮，任親戚求財，丘和進食邀幸，皆無取焉。

translations.literal: Ren Gui indulged a jealous wife without propriety and allowed relatives to seek wealth; Qiu He advanced food to court favor—all are without what is to be taken as exemplary.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui indulged a jealous wife without propriety and allowed relatives to seek wealth; Qiu He advanced food to court favor—all are without what is to be taken as exemplary.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：屈突守節，求仁得仁。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Qu held to integrity and, seeking benevolence, obtained benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Qu held to integrity and, seeking benevolence, obtained it.

sentences.zh: 諸君遇主，不足擬倫。

translations.literal: The various lords in meeting their sovereign are not enough to be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: The others, in meeting their sovereign, cannot be compared with him.
